articles.title: Drama galore at US Open as Alex de Minuar dudded and top seeds crash out
articles.excerpt: More big names have been sent packing. Read more here.
articles.content:
The Aussie tennis star has copped a rough hand at Flushing Meadows.

Alex de Minaur will have to play three times in three days - and seven matches in 12 days if he wants to win the US Open - after some scheduling chaos for the Aussie at the US Open. And Wednesday's action (local time) was rocked by some big names crashing out and a pretty dire day for the rest of the Aussies.

De Minaur comfortably cleared his first hurdle at Flushing Meadows with a 6-2 6-2 6-4 victory over Andrea Guerrieri. But the Aussie tennis star has been completely dudded by the schedule and wet weather in New York.

Andrey Rublev (L) and Rafael Jodar (R) both crashed out, while Alex de Minaur (centre) advanced but has a brutal schedule. Image: Getty/ESPN

De Minaur was originally slated to play his first-round match on day three of the tournament, which is already a tricky situation considering other players have been resting up since winning on day one. But the Aussie's match was then pushed to day four due to wet weather on Tuesday night.

The World No.7's match finally got underway on Wednesday, but was then suspended for over an hour due to more rain. He eventually prevailed and advanced comfortably, but his schedule has suddenly become very tricky.

The Aussie star will play again on Thursday (Friday Aussie time) against 70th-ranked Botic van de Zandschulp, and will have to play three matches in three days if he wins through. If he manages to make the final in New York he'll have to play seven best-of-five matches in the space of just 12 days.

To sum up the chaos that de Minaur has endured, Daniil Medvedev and Alex Michelsen had already won their second-round matches BEFORE the Aussie had even stepped on court for his first. It means de Minaur will face a distinct disadvantage in not having as much rest as some rivals.

Alex de Minaur was too good for Andrea Guerrieri at the US Open. (Photo by Pete Staples/USTA via Getty Images)

More seeded players crash out of US Open

The draw was blown wide open on Wednesday when seeded players Rafael Jodar (12), Brandon Nakashima (16) and Andrey Rublev (23) all crashed out. Jodar lost his first-round match to Yunchaokete Bu, while Rublev and Nakashima lost in the second round - to Michelsen and Daniel Merida Aguilar respectively.

They joined Novak Djokovic (4), Arthur Fils (10), Cameron Norrie (29) and Matteo Arnaldi (30) as seeded men to crash out early, while Casper Ruud (19) withdrew before his first match. On the women's side, Jelana Ostapenko (30) lost to Tatjana Maria, joining other big-name casualties in Belinda Bencic (12), Maja Chwalinska (20), Barbora Krejcikova (27) and Sara Bejlek (28).

For the Aussie contingent, Daria Kasatkina lost to Paula Badosa in a match that was postponed overnight with Badosa only two points away from victory. Taylah Preston was no match for Taylor Townsend, losing 6-1 6-1 in just 48 minutes, while Kim Birrell went down to Ekaterina Alexandrova in three.

James Duckworth joined the Aussie exits with a straight-sets loss to Wu Yibing. And Maya Joint took a set off ninth seed Elina Svitolina but ultimately fell 2-6 6-7 4-4.

Few actors have had a career like Michael B. Jordan has, as he has accomplished quite a bit within the entertainment industry. Jordan started as a child actor and, after years of rising through the ranks in Hollywood, he now headlines massive movies. One of his most recent films – the critically acclaimed Sinners – even landed Jordan an Oscar. The fan-favorite star is certainly thriving as a performer, but I really think we need to take some time and admire how he's thriving apart from his on-camera career.

Credit: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Pictures Inc/Eli Ade

Michael B. Jordan Is Proving Himself To Be A Talented Director

August is Black Business Month, so I thought this would be the perfect occasion to highlight the incredible trajectory Jordan has had, specifically his non-acting ventures. Over the past few years, what's impressed me is the way in which he's jumped into the director's chair. The star made his directorial debut with 2023's Creed III, the third installment in the Rocky spinoff franchise he's headlined.

I was excited to see what Jordan would do with the threequel, and he definitely didn't disappoint. Creed III received positive reviews, with much of that praise going towards the story, performances and of course, Jordan's direction. Sure, he gives a great performance as Adonis Creed, but what really impressed me was the star's desire to add his anime-inspired sensibilities to the boxing scenes (and shoot them with IMAX cameras). The film is a knockout, and Jordan can now take that momentum into his next directorial effort.

A legacy sequel was ambitious enough, but Jordan has since helmed and produced a remake of The Thomas Crown Affair, which is set to hit theaters amid the 2027 movie schedule. Jordan is also set to play the titular billionaire/art thief and, based on the first Thomas Crown trailer, he's cooked up a film that oozes intrigue, charm and sensuality. I'm hopeful that the movie will be another solid notch in Jordan's belt and allow him the chance to direct even more down the road.

Credit: Amazon MGM Studios

Producing Has Also Become A Part Of Michael B. Jordan's Career

Jordan has also become a producer and, in 2016, he even founded his own production company, Outlier Society, in 2016. When it comes to movies, Jordan has produced films like Just Mercy, Without Remorse, A Journal for Jordan and Creed III. The producing work isn't limited to the silver screen either, as the multihyphenate has also served as an executive producer on TV shows, from Raising Dion and David Makes Man to Gen: Lock and the upcoming Fourth Wing adaptation.

So I think it's safe to say that Michael B. Jordan has his fingerprints on a growing list of Hollywood productions. If that weren't enough, he's also moved into sports ownership and has embarked on a few key ventures. He became a part-owner of the AFC Bournemouth English soccer club in 2022, and he has also invested in the Alpine F1 team. I have to wonder, where does this man find the time to manage all of these obligations?

In all seriousness, though, it's awe-inspiring to see what Jordan has accomplished and at a relatively young age. Honestly, I'd be impressed with seeing just about anyone reach such heights, but watching a Black man do that in a historically unpredictable industry is particularly satisfying for me. He's come a long way since The Wire and even his breakthrough movie role in Fruitvale Station, and I look forward to seeing what he does – both on and off screen – as his profile continues to rise.

And don't worry, Jordan will surely continue to be an actor. Check him out when The Thomas Crown Affair opens on March 5, 2027, and he's landed another big franchise with Miami Vice '85, which will be released in 2028.

Plans have been submitted for seven new outdoor padel courts to be built at a retail park.

Soul Padel has applied to Sunderland City Council for permission to develop a vacant plot at Peel Retail Park in Washington.

The company said a similar plan for the site had already been previously approved, but they were now reducing the number of courts from nine to seven and allowing space for extra parking.

The site, which is currently a plot of grassland, would also include two shipping containers to be used as a clubhouse, changing rooms and cafe bar.

Planning documents said Soul Padel was an operator specialising in development and management of padel courts across the UK.

"Its mission is to make padel an inclusive and sociable sport, encouraging participation from people of all ages, backgrounds and abilities," the documents said.

Plans show the padel courts would have fabric canopies over a steel structure to protect them from the weather for year-round use.

Soul Padel said it believed the development would "make a valuable contribution to the health and wellbeing of residents" in the area.

It added: "Overall, the proposed development represents a positive and beneficial use of underutilised land, delivering modern, accessible and much-needed sports facilities for the local community."

Sunderland City Council is expected to make a decision in due course.

articles.title: Michael B. Jordan: 4 Viral Clips Fans Keep Watching (September 2026)
articles.excerpt: Michael B. Jordan dominates screens from Creed III to Black Panther. Discover the standout viral moments and interviews fans replay endlessly.
articles.content:
From sci-fi superpower theories to boxing ring directorship, explore Michael B. Jordan's most replayed highlights.

Michael B. Jordan continues to captivate fans across social feeds with unforgettable roles in Black Panther, Creed III, and classic early interviews.

When Michael B. Jordan sat down with Young Hollywood early in his film career, his presence pointed directly toward future blockbuster dominion. Long before steering massive studio franchises or directing tentpole films, Jordan was establishing an undeniable screen rhythm that audiences immediately latched onto. His early turns demonstrated a performer who understood physical nuance, whether playing troubled high school athletes or young men discovering sudden supernatural abilities.

Having covered Jordan across 300 stories since 2009, Young Hollywood tracked his evolution from critically acclaimed television roles to full creative autonomy under his Outlier Society production banner. His career trajectory combines relentless physical discipline with a sharp eye for commanding screen presence, generating scenes that fans continually pull apart and replay across social video platforms. Watch our full sit-down with Michael B. Jordan below.

Exploring Superpowers and Lucasfilm Archives

Jordan's breakout leading turn in 2012 saw him tackling complex young characters navigating sudden power and high-stakes military history. During his visits to sets backed by legendary filmmakers like George Lucas, Jordan seized every chance to absorb cinematic history up close. He recalled looking through iconic props before filming even began.

"Oh, definitely. So I definitely. Oh, George, can we see the archives before we get to work and so I definitely saw you like R2D2 and like you know Chewy and all the Stormtroopers," Michael B. Jordan told Young Hollywood about visiting the Lucasfilm headquarters.

The conversation naturally drifted toward the superhuman abilities at the center of his sci-fi breakout. When asked about the reality of mind-bending powers, Jordan brought an earnest enthusiasm to the premise while weighing in on which power he would actually pick for himself.

"I think telekinesis is definitely plausible. I think if you know, certain people, I don't know, maybe born with a gift," Jordan explained. When pressed on his own ideal personal upgrade, his answer arrived without hesitation: "Maybe like super speed. Like being able to like, I don't know, to go as fast as I want like Flash."

The Museum Confrontation in Black Panther

In 2018, Jordan stepped into Marvel's Black Panther as Erik Killmonger, delivering one of the most compelling antagonist performances in comic book movie history. His entry into the film's museum scene immediately went viral for its calculated poise, sharp styling, and utter refusal to compromise. Dressed in modern tactical streetwear, Killmonger turned a simple gallery inquiry into a gripping exposition of colonial history and personal reckoning.

Fans quickly clipped the sequence, circulating Jordan's icy smirk and measured vocal cadences across video platforms. Killmonger did not operate like a cartoonish supervillain; Jordan infused him with righteous anger, physical menace, and emotional depth. That specific museum sequence established a visual benchmark that modern franchise villains still struggle to match, turning a single dialogue scene into a repeatable pop landmark.

Directorial Precision in Creed III

Jordan did not merely reprise his role as Adonis Creed for 2023's Creed III; he stepped into the director's chair to reshape the boxing franchise's visual language. Drawing inspiration from classic Japanese animation, Jordan designed combat sequences that emphasized speed, impact frames, and intense psychological focus. Instead of standard sports movie choreography, the climactic ring battles felt heightened, brutal, and deeply personal.

Behind-the-scenes clips of Jordan calling shots in the ring while wearing boxing gloves became an instant hit with audiences who love filmmaking craft. The training montages, featuring grueling beach runs and heavyweight tire pulls, immediately took over fitness feeds. Fans marveled at how smoothly Jordan balanced rigorous physical conditioning with the creative demands of steering a multi-million-dollar production, proving his command over both sides of the camera lens.

The Television Foundations That Built a Powerhouse

The dramatic weight Jordan brings to blockbusters traces straight back to his unforgettable television work. Audiences first felt his emotional gravity as the vulnerable Wallace on The Wire, a performance that anchored one of the drama's most heartbreaking narrative arcs. He later carried Friday Night Lights through its final seasons as quarterback Vince Howard, demonstrating his ability to lead an ensemble cast with raw charisma.

Those foundational drama roles established a credibility that stayed with him as he expanded his creative reach. Through his Outlier Society production company, Jordan now develops original television concepts and major feature films, ensuring diverse creators receive authentic studio backing. He transitioned from an exceptional young ensemble talent into an industry heavyweight who shapes the projects he stars in.

Whether revisiting his early thoughts on superhuman speed or admiring the intricate fight choreography he orchestrated in the ring, Jordan continues to generate scenes that demand repeat viewing. His career demonstrates what happens when genuine craft meets unyielding ambition. For fans following his trajectory across two decades, every new performance feels like another chapter in a legendary run.

articles.title: Catherine Zeta-Jones uses Welsh accent in new Amazon series Kill Jackie
articles.excerpt: The Hollywood actress is starring in a new thriller series using her natural Swansea accent.
articles.content:
This will be Zeta-Jones's first major screen role using a Welsh accent

  • Published
    5 hours ago

Catherine Zeta-Jones has been praised by fans as she uses her natural Welsh accent in an upcoming thriller series.

The 56-year-old Hollywood actor returned to her hometown of Swansea, where some of the filming took place for Amazon's Kill Jackie.

A trailer released on social media gives viewers their first glimpse of the show, as well as a snippet of Zeta-Jones using her Swansea accent.

The Oscar-winning star plays Jackie Price, an extravagant jet-setter who is trying to stay anonymous after escaping a "dangerous past as an international cocaine dealer," according to Amazon Prime.

One fan said they loved hearing the "queen of Wales sounding Welsh".

Óscar Jaenada as Zigor and Catherine Zeta-Jones as Jackie Price in Kill Jackie

The series is based on the novel The Price You Pay by Nick Harkaway, published under his pseudonym Aidan Truhen.

Bilbao, Lisbon and London were also used as filming locations.

Zeta-Jones is known for an array of previous roles including Morticia Addams in Netflix's Wednesday, and an Oscar-winning supporting role in Chicago.

Kill Jackie will be her first major role using her Welsh accent.

She has previously spoken about her strong connection to Wales, adding in her heart she "never really left".

One fan commented on an Instagram post of the trailer, saying "her Welsh is out and I love it, can't wait".

Zeta-Jones said she had been looking forward to the opportunity to explore a female-driven plot that "encompasses empowerment, identity and redemption".

Damon Thomas, of Killing Eve, also stars in the show while Gangs Of London's Tom Butterworth is the writer and showrunner of the series.

Kill Jackie will premiere on 2 October on Amazon Prime

Thirteen climbers are set to make their international debut, while South Korea’s Kim Ja In approaches an important milestone

The World Climbing Series Koper 2026 is the 426th World Cup or World Climbing Series event in history, as well as the 241st Lead competition for both women and men. It is the fifth event to be held in Koper and the 33rd in Slovenia.

A total of 147 athletes from 37 nations across five continents are registered to compete. Bosnia and Herzegovina will be represented at a World Cup or World Climbing Series event for the first time.

ATHLETES’ HIGHLIGHTS

South Korea’s Kim Ja In is set to make her 110th Lead competition start. She currently ranks third on the all-time list, behind Austria’s Barbara Bacher with 116 starts and Italy’s Jenny Lavarda with 112. Austria’s Jessica Pilz will make her 63rd Lead start, while home favourite Janja Garnbret will make her 53rd.

Jakob Schubert is approaching his 100th Lead competition start, with Koper marking his 91st. He sits third in the men’s all-time ranking behind Spain’s Ramón Julian Puigblanque with 129 starts and France’s Romain Desgranges with 117.

Germany’s Sebastian Halenke will become his country’s record holder for the most Lead competition starts, reaching 59 and overtaking Christian Bindhammer.

Stefan Bajcetic has shared a poignant farewell message after his permanent departure from Liverpool FC this week.

The midfielder completed a transfer back to former team Celta Vigo on Monday, after five-and-a-half years on Merseyside.

A rapid ascent through the Reds’ Academy saw Bajcetic debut at senior level in August 2022 and go on to enjoy a breakthrough season.

However, injury setbacks prevented him from building on that advancement in the campaigns that followed.

His time at Anfield concluded with totals of 22 appearances and one goal.

“Dear Liverpool fans, I never planned to write a goodbye message, because I was where I always wanted to be,” he posted on social media today.

“The love you have given me throughout the five years I spent in Liverpool has been incredible. It’s easy to show love when things go in the right direction, but as you know it hasn’t always been the case with me, and you have been there for me at all times.

“I fought all the injuries and adversities with the motivation of paying back the love and trust you showed me over this period, but unfortunately, I couldn’t.

“In life sometimes you need a change and thinking of myself and my family I think it’s time. The memories I’ve had with this club will stay with me forever and I’m glad I will be able to tell my kids I played in the best club in England.

“We will never know what could have been but my period here has helped me mature and grow as a person and as a player, from what I was when I arrived at 16 to now it’s a completely different person.

“I lived with a Scouse family that showed me how special this city and people are, and I can proudly say I will always have a little bit of that in me.

“So thank you for everything from the bottom of my heart, me and my family will always be Reds.

“To all my teammates, from the ones I had in the U16s, U18s, U21s to the first team, everyone has helped me so much over the years and I keep friends for life. Playing with you guys has been such a privilege and a constant learning experience. Thank you for always helping me.

“To the staff and managers I had over the years, each one of you helped me develop so much.

“This club is a massive family and it wouldn’t be without all the people that work for it, from chefs, kitchen staff, player care, groundskeepers, media, kit men, and all the hundred departments this club has, everyone makes our life so much easier and keeps this club as big as it is. I will miss you so much.

“Physios, doctors, medical department, what can I say? Unfortunately, we got to spend so much time together, we lived so many ups and downs, and you have always given your best for me. I will always be grateful.

“This club will stay in my heart forever.

“Once a Red, forever a Red.”

2nd September 26

Halloween: The Game was designed to offer rich player progression, satisfying rewards, and robust customization. From compelling character cosmetic items to meaningful gameplay unlocks, our team has strived to ensure your time in Haddonfield is commended. While we’ve previously highlighted various elements of the metagame experience in our asymmetrical horror sandbox, we are thrilled to demonstrate what players can look forward to from the horrifying hook of Halloween: The Game.

Whether you’re diving into the singleplayer story mode, private matches against AI, or online 1v4 matchmaking, Halloween: The Game offers a feast of challenges to chase and a nearly endless number of milestones to achieve. We’re delivering players Passive + Progressive Challenges for both Michael and Civilians, Singleplayer Story Mode Challenges to encourage replayability, comprehensive character customization, customizable player profile cards, four levels of player progression, and a rollable perk card system complete with decks and an earnable currency. Completionists have their work cut out for them.

By completing matches or enjoying the singleplayer story mode, players earn experience points that are applied to four distinct categories of Player Progression Levels: Profile Level, Killer Level, Civilian Level, and Weapon Level. Profile Level encompasses all gained XP regardless of which role you choose to play. Killer Level is earned by becoming the Boogeyman and terrorizing the residents of Haddonfield. Civilian Level is tied to each playable Civilian character. And Weapon Level is earned by dispatching victims with specific equipable weapons as Michael.

Growing your Player Progression Levels unlocks additional playable Civilian characters, new Michael abilities, supplemental Starting Items for Civilians, cosmetic rewards, new tiers of challenges, executions, and more. Dedicated players can also prestige upon reaching the max progression level in any of these four categories to chase additional rewards and flex their achievements.

Passive + Progressive Challenges

In addition to Player Progression Levels, Halloween: The Game features an extensive suite of Passive and Progressive Challenges. Passive Challenges are divided into multiple categories for both Killer and Civilian roles and are automatically tracked regardless of which character you select. Progressive Challenges are tied to specific Civilian characters, Michael Skins, and weapon types, and players are tasked with tackling these objectives in succession to unlock rewards.

Singleplayer Challenges

Our singleplayer story mode also provides optional challenges for all six playable chapters that unlock alternate outfits and unique cosmetic items, including a legendary look for committed Boogeymen who complete every singleplayer challenge. Between Passive, Progressive, and optional singleplayer objectives, Halloween: The Game is packed with 100s of challenges for horror fans to chase.

Upon gaining Player Progression Levels and completing challenges, players will earn a satisfying suite of options for customizing Michael Myers and Civilians.

Michael Customization

Michael loadouts come equipped with two starting traits - Killer Sense and Shape Jump, which provide essential tools for stalking and slaying the residents of Haddonfield. From there, players can customize Michael’s appearance with Killer Skins and Tints, unlock and select new starting weapons with earnable tints, and choose three distinct Michael abilities such as Reality Tear, Blackout, Detection Pulse, and more.

Civilian Customization

Civilian Characters offer their own unique stats and signature traits, making your choices incredibly important when facing off against the Shape of Evil. Civilian loadouts allow you to customize each character’s appearance, including outfits with multiple tints, hair/headwear, eyewear, and makeup/blemishes, unlockable starting items, and Civilian Perk Decks.

Athleticism
Athleticism determines how quickly and efficiently a Civilian moves through Haddonfield on foot or by bike.

Personality
Personality affects a Civilian's ability to convince residents, alert the authorities, and command additional followers, as well as determine their Fear and Stalk resistances.

Resourcefulness
Resourcefulness determines a Civilian's repair expertise, environmental awareness, and competence when operating motor vehicles or firearms.

Capability
Capability represents a Civilian's overall vigor and prowess when wielding melee weapons or throwable household items.

As an added layer of customization, Halloween: The Game will also feature fully adjustable Player Profile Cards. By increasing their Player Progression Levels and completing challenges, players earn Profile Icons, Profile Backgrounds, and Profile Titles that can be used to build Profile Cards. There are dozens of options to choose from, and these personalized Profile Cards add extra flair to the online multiplayer experience.

Civilian Perk Cards enable players to craft their very own Perk Decks. Completing matches supplies Perk Points, which can be used to roll for Perk Cards that provide varying levels of gameplay boosts within matches. To increase their odds of pulling higher-rarity cards, players can choose to spend greater amounts of Perk Points during rolls. Players can also use Perk Points to temporarily upgrade cards they own, which increases their level for a set number of matches. Once players have amassed a solid collection of Perk Cards, they can construct Perk Decks which can be equipped to Civilian Loadouts. The randomized in-game Perk Card rolls ensure no two matches of Halloween: The Game play out the same.

The Runner is not winning over critics as it sprints onto Prime Video. The new action thriller starring Wonder Woman star Gal Gadot debuted to just 9% on Rotten Tomatoes, becoming the actor's lowest-ranked movie.

Directed by Kevin Macdonald, the movie stars Gadot as an attorney who must race through London on the orders of a mysterious caller to save her abducted son. Damien Lewis also stars in the movie, which is now available to stream on Prime Video.

The Guardian gives it just two stars, adding: "Intelligence might not be what one would expect here, which is somewhat acceptable in B-movie territory such as this, but the lack of excitement is hard to forgive."

Not all the reviews are bad. Jordan Mintzer of The Hollywood Reporter argues: "Movies such as these are all about suspension of disbelief, and The Runner keeps a fast enough pace that we don't wind up asking too many questions."

On the press tour for the new film, Gadot has been making headlines about her Wonder Woman exit. The star, who played the superhero in the DCEU, says she wasn't told the full picture by James Gunn and Peter Safran when they took over as DC Studios CEOs.

articles.excerpt: Body found in ravine after Alexander Harris failed to arrive at hotel
articles.content:
Body found in ravine after Alexander Harris failed to arrive at hotel

The body of a British consultant who went missing on a hike in Pakistan has been found.

Alexander Harris, 30, scaled the 13,000ft Musa Ka Musala mountain in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Saturday with his friend Alun David Cooper Cledwyn.

The pair took photographs at the summit and then took separate routes down the mountain, police said.

Mr Harris, a dual British and Irish citizen from Birmingham, failed to return to the hotel, prompting a search operation.

Khalid Iqbal, the Mansehra deputy police commissioner, told the BBC that the body had been found on a path in a forested ravine after an extensive search.

Mr Iqbal said it was suspected that Mr Harris had slipped and fallen after it began raining.

The area where the body was found includes narrow ravines, dangerous mountain tracks and steep drops, and is particularly treacherous in wet weather.

Between 250 and 300 police officers, shepherds familiar with the terrain and other members of the public had searched for Mr Harris on foot and with drones.

Mr Harris, who lived in Islamabad, was an experienced trekker who had climbed Musa Ka Musala before, and frequently travelled to different locations in the region to hike.

Mr Harris and Mr Cledwyn were staying in Siran Valley and began the climb without informing the authorities or obtaining the relevant paperwork, officials said.

Mr Iqbal said: “The hotel had offered him a guide and police security, but he said that he knew the area and did not need any help.”

‘Cared deeply for Pakistan’

Mr Harris worked for Adam Smith International, the global aid and development consultancy, in Pakistan.

A spokesman for the company said: “He cared deeply for Pakistan, its people, its nature, and learned Urdu during his time there.

“We are deeply grateful to the hundreds of people who joined the search effort, including local residents, volunteers, police, rescue teams, forest department, members of Alex’s trail-running community and the government of Pakistan that supported the operation.

“They searched tirelessly in difficult conditions, often in heavy rain, fog and poor visibility, over steep and challenging terrain.

“Our thoughts are with Alex’s family, friends and colleagues at this incredibly difficult time. We remain focused on supporting his family.”

Mr Harris was a keen runner and his running group posted multiple pleas for information while he was missing.

Breaking the news, Islamabad Run With Us wrote on Instagram: “It is with deep sadness that we share the news that Alex’s body has been found in Paracha jungle.

“After days of search and rescue efforts, this is a heartbreaking outcome for his family, friends and everyone who was hoping and praying for his safe return.”

A Foreign Office spokesman said: “We are supporting the family of a British man who has died in Pakistan and are in contact with the local authorities.”

Alexander Harris went missing on Saturday as he descended from the summit of Musa Ka Musala

  • Published

The body of a British trekker has been found in northern Pakistan, local officials have said.

Alexander Harris, who was originally from Birmingham, went missing on Saturday as he was descending from the summit of Musa Ka Musala, a mountain of just over 4,000m (13,000ft), in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

Khalid Iqbal, the area's deputy commissioner, said police and volunteers had been involved in a search for 30-year-old Harris and his body was found on a path in a forest, adding "most probably he slipped and fell".

He had been living in Pakistan's capital Islamabad where he worked for global advisory company Adam Smith International.

A Foreign Office spokesperson said it was "supporting the family of a British man who has died in Pakistan and are in contact with the local authorities".

Harris, who also had Irish citizenship, had set off on the trek around 05:40 local time on Saturday with a hiking companion. They took some photos at the summit and then began to descend, before becoming separated.

"There was a difference in their speed," Iqbal said. "He [Harris] was moving faster, he got about 1-2km ahead. Then it started raining."

The deputy commissioner estimated that between 250-300 people were involved in the rescue operation including police and volunteers, searching on foot and with drones, although their use was limited by poor visibility.

A keen hiker and trail runner, Harris was a regular participant in long distance races in Pakistan.

Iqbal said the two trekkers had not told the authorities about the trip.

"The hotel had offered him a guide and police security," Iqbal says. "But he said that he knew the area and did not need any help."

Alexander Harris had been working for a global advisory company in Islamabad

In a statement, Adam Smith International said Harris was a "much loved member" of their team and that they were devastated by his death.

His company said: "He cared deeply for Pakistan, its people, its nature, and learned Urdu during his time there."

It added: "We are deeply grateful to the hundreds of people who joined the search effort, including local residents, volunteers, police, rescue teams, forest department, members of Alex's trail running community, and the government of Pakistan that supported the operation.

"They searched tirelessly in difficult conditions, often in heavy rain, fog and poor visibility, over steep and challenging terrain."

It said: "Our thoughts are with Alex's family, friends and colleagues at this incredibly difficult time. We remain focused on supporting his family."

Harris's running group, Margalla Trail Runners, posted on social media calling him "a passionate trail runner".

They added: "May his soul rest in peace and may his family and loved ones find strength and comfort during this difficult time."

Sky Bet odds | Paddy Power | Betfair

A meeting of Edinburgh's two major sides who have both started the new season in positive enough fashion. Hibernian and Hearts have two wins apiece from three on their respective records with the latter securing a spot in a European competition too.

Concerns about Hearts undergoing life post-Derek McInnes came to the fore when Austrian outfit Sturm Graz convincingly beat them over two legs in Champions League qualification, followed by a similar outcome from Benfica in the Europa League - an opening day league defeat to Aberdeen sandwiched in between the two ties as well.

But since the 6-1 thrashing in Portugal they've embarked on a six-game unbeaten run across all competitions which includes a successful return to Austria to beat Rapid Wien over two legs to reach the group stage of the Conference League. A strong first-half performance against St. Johnstone last time out deserved more than the 2-1 victory they eventually secured.

Hibs have also endured mixed fortunes as another side whose campaign began in mid-July. An abysmal defeat to Malisheva from Kosovo kicked things off in the worst possible fashion but they overcame them in the home leg. Since then, six of eight outings have returned at least a draw.

Not only is this an Edinburgh derby but it's also a contest between two sides who have demonstrated strength in attack so far. Across the three league games both Hibs and Hearts sit in the top four in terms of the quality of chances created, with Celtic (obviously) and Dundee United (who have been behind a lot and played a game extra) the only teams with higher expected goals (xG) figures.

What's pleasing about the number from a Hearts perspective is that they've spent the large majority of their three games in the lead. In fact, no side has led more than the 82% of the game time seen by Wouter Vrancken's outfit. That will make the loss at Aberdeen even more frustrating given the nature of it.

They've only trailed for a matter of seconds. Hibs, meanwhile, have only been behind for around 21 minutes in the league so far. Some may therefore point to the draw, which is of course a very realistic possibility, but I'm instead settling for OVER 2.5 GOALS at just shy of even money.

The above is there to add context to the underlying numbers and why they're in fact stronger than other teams, even if some may boast a higher figure. Despite being ahead, both sides still push to create chances and don't simply rest on what they have.

A stats-based angle I was interested in was the over 28.5 shots at around 6/4. This has the feel of quite an open game anyway without even factoring in the derby crowd element to it - Hibs could only muster four shots in their meeting in April so almost 'owe it' to their supporters to improve anyway.

Eight of Hearts' ten competitive games this season have gone over 2.5 with one of those which didn't being the home draw with Benfica, a game which was played with the tie already decided given the outcome in Portugal.

Two players I'd focus on from a shots-perspective though are Hibs' Josh Mulligan and Hearts' Blair Spittal given their previous showings. The former available at 7/4 with Hills for an effort on target. While it wouldn't have mattered here if it was a staked selection, I'll still point out that it's worth checking with your chosen bookmaker as some don't offer the 'super sub' promotion in the Scottish Premiership.

I'm keeping it simple by backing goals instead, in what should hopefully be a highly-entertaining Edinburgh derby.

articles.content:
Your essential guide to the line-up of RuPaul's Drag Race UK.

  • Katelyn Mensah

Mama Ru is back in action tonight as RuPaul's Drag Race UK returns for its eighth season on BBC Three, introducing audiences to a new group of queens who will stop at nothing to win the title of the UK's Next Drag Race Superstar.

Over 10 weeks, the queens will tackle a series of challenges designed to test every corner of their drag skill-set, from runway looks to lip-sync battles. As ever, the winner of the week takes home a coveted RuPeter badge, while the bottom two face a deciding 'Lip Sync For Their Life' and the risk of elimination.

This year's cast spans the country and the drag spectrum, from a Belfast marine-biology mermaid to a Darlington boardroom "businesswoman", and includes Lucky Roy Singh, who is the first Sikh South Asian queen to compete on Drag Race UK.

Here's a guide to the contestants taking part this season.

RuPaul's Drag Race UK season 8 full line-up

Below is a list of the contestants confirmed to be taking part in RuPaul's Drag Race UK season 8.

  • Alik
  • Anita Piss
  • Coral-Hole Mandi
  • The Delta Quadrant
  • Flesh
  • KY Kelly
  • Lucky Roy Singh
  • ma_danni_x
  • Mocha
  • Naya Thorn
  • Paris Baby
  • Tequila Thirst

Read on to learn more about the contestants taking part.

Alik

Age: 29

Location: Brighton

Pronouns in drag: She/Her

Alik has been doing drag for eight years and describes her aesthetic as "old meets new", a goth-glamour and punk melting pot born out of Brighton's club scene.

A former trampolinist and gymnast, she promises flips, tricks and dips, and is determined to break the so-called "Brighton curse" that has dogged the city's queens on the show. She is in a relationship with season 1's Scaredy Kat and says she is competing partly as their "redemption", living vicariously through her run.

Anita Piss

Age: 37

Location: Birmingham

Pronouns in drag: She/Her

Originally from Birmingham but forged in the subversive East London drag scene, Anita Piss finally landed a place after applying five times. She has been doing drag for around "seven or eight years" and only recently went full-time.

With Jamaican and British heritage and a lifelong love of fashion, she promises a "cool, calm and collected" approach and plenty of poise as she looks to bring something different to the werkroom.

Coral-Hole Mandi

Age: 27

Location: Belfast

Pronouns in drag: She/Her

The self-described "Bikini Bottom Bimbo", Coral-Hole Mandi is originally from Ballymena and now based in Belfast. Her drag draws on a background in marine biology and a love of the sea, swinging between candy-coloured cartoon mermaid and "bog witch" creature of the deep. After around six years in drag, the "loud" and competitive queen is hoping to snatch the crown for Belfast.

The Delta Quadrant

Age: 32

Location: Darlington

Pronouns in drag: She/Her

Dubbed as "the Deborah Meaden of drag", The Delta Quadrant is a character-led queen whose persona is a Darlington business tycoon and "CEO of everything". She favours a single signature look built on power dressing, shoulder pads, tailored suits and a sharp bob.

She admits the sewing challenge makes her nervous but is out to prove that comedy, character-led drag deserves a place on the world stage.

Flesh

Age: 25

Location: London

Pronouns in drag: She/Her

The self-described "supermodel of Soho", Flesh has been in drag for seven years and takes her cues from 1990s supermodels and British fashion. With Spanish heritage and an Oxford English literature degree, she blends high-glamour poise with party-girl energy.

She is close to reigning Drag Race UK winner Bones, with whom she performs as "Flesh and Bones", and counts Krystal Versace and DeDeLicious among her drag family.

Ky Kelly

Age: 42

Location: Staffordshire

Pronouns in drag: She/Her

A live-singing comedy diva from Rugeley, Ky Kelly has spent nearly 16 years on the cabaret circuit, performing up and down the country and on cruises. She recently appeared in Everybody's Talking About Jamie, which she calls the best experience of her life. "Bold, brash and sassy", she is flying the flag for older, more mature divas and the cabaret scene.

Lucky Roy Singh

Age: 36

Location: Manchester

Pronouns in drag: She/Her

Lucky Roy Singh is the first Sikh South Asian queen on Drag Race UK, describing herself as a "Bollywood Punjabi diva" whose "East meets West" aesthetic draws on culture, heritage and history. She has been performing for over a decade and is also an award-winning activist, with campaigning work around domestic abuse and honour-based abuse.

Attitude reports she was honoured at the 2019 Attitude Pride Awards for her advocacy. She says a win would mean the world to her and to the British South Asian community.

ma_danni_x

Age: 48

Location: The Wirral

Pronouns in drag: She/Her

The "squirrel from the Wirral", ma_danni_x brings 28 years of drag experience, having started at 21 as a cruise-ship dancer before landing an early job at Soho's Madame JoJo's.

She says she has shared stages and screens with names including Lily Savage, George Michael and Samantha Fox, and previously appeared on Britain's Got Talent. Now based in West London, she calls a place on Drag Race UK a dream come true.

Mocha

Age: 26

Location: Essex

Pronouns in drag: She/Her

Originally from Essex and now working the London scene, Mocha describes her drag as "Soho perfection blended with East London grit", leaning vintage and showgirl with a cartoonish streak and a love of musical theatre.

She says she auditioned for all eight seasons before getting in and is a skilled seamstress who makes looks for other queens as well as herself.

Naya Thorn

Age: 24

Location: Dudley

Pronouns in drag: She/Her

Now based in Manchester after starting out in Liverpool, Naya Thorn is a theatrical performer who builds her shows around emotional, meaningful song choices.

Fiercely competitive, she admits werkroom friendships may take a back seat to her ambition, and says she has taken sewing classes to prepare for the design challenge.

Paris Baby

Age: 27

Location: Hastings

Pronouns in drag: She/Her

The "British Bajan Barbie", Paris Baby is a fierce lip-syncer with seven years in drag, promising tricks, splits, flips and plenty of drama. Drawing on her Barbadian heritage and inspirations from TLC and Destiny's Child to Paris Hilton, she positions herself as the villain the UK has been waiting for and is eyeing the girl group challenge and the roast.

Tequila Thirst

Age: 39

Location: London

Pronouns in drag: She/Her

Originally from North London and now living in Chester, Tequila Thirst is a bright, high-energy host, singer and dancer who came to drag through cosplay and Comic Con.

A Vietnamese North Londoner, she leans into juicy greens, hot pinks and bright citrus colours, and says she is most excited about the girl group challenge.

articles.title: RuPaul's Drag Race UK: Belfast diva ready to take series 'by the horns'
articles.excerpt: Coral-Hole Mandi is the only contestant from Northern Ireland on this series of RuPaul's Drag Race UK, which starts on Thursday.
articles.content:
"It's now or never" for Coral-Hole Mandi who is ready to compete in series eight of RuPaul's Drag Race UK

  • Published
    2 September 2026

It's time to start your engines. The new series of Ru Paul's Drag Race UK is about to start and contestant Coral-Hole Mandi is ready to "take it by the horns" and "give it everything".

The 27-year-old calls herself the Bikini Bottom Bimbo from Belfast and she is the only contestant from Northern Ireland in this season.

She is one of 12 contestants hoping to impress Mama Ru and Michelle Visage.

Her plans for doing that?

"I'm going to be the fully realised, colourful cartoon diva that I've always dreamed of being."

Mandi works in Belfast and loves "how alternative the Belfast drag scene is".

"No performer does the same thing in Belfast. Everyone has their own little niche. There's a lot of campy showgirly drag. There's a lot of old school divas. There's a lot of new age, more alternative drag, club kids and creatures as well.

"Any corner you look, there is every variety of drag in Belfast and it's amazing.

She thinks that should be celebrated more and that Belfast "probably has one of the most diverse drag scenes in the UK, but not a lot of Belfast drag has been represented".

Mandi thinks casting two queens from Belfast on the same season would allow them to "bounce off each other".

"I think that's the only way that you're going to get the authentic Northern Irish craic," she said.

Ru Paul loves the Irish, according to Mandi

Although Mandi is a "Belfast diva through and through", she is originally from Ballymena.

"There's not too many drag performers from Ballymena," she said, adding that there were some "culchie divas".

"They have a different personality, a different sense of craic than city people from Belfast," she said.

"It's like country charm, maybe."

'Creature of the Black Drag-oon'

Mandi studied marine biology and spent time in Indonesia studying coral reefs, which has inspired her act.

"My drag is very aquatic, creature of the deep, like marine biology, fish, mermaids, all of that stuff combined in one," she said.

"But I also like anything that's colourful, kaleidoscopic, and like crayons, I'm not afraid to play with all the colours in the pot.

"I always call myself the creature of the Black Dragoon."

Michelle Visage and Alan Carr are judges in RuPaul's Drag Race UK

For anyone new to RuPaul's Drag Race, a group of drag queens compete against each other by completing weekly challenges, like putting together edgy looks and performing lip sync battles.

Although Mandi does not describe herself as a singer or a dancer, she can "belt a note in the shower and in the car", so is looking forward to Rusical week where contestants sing, dance and act in a drag-themed production.

"I never thought in a million years that I'd be on the Drag Race main stage," she said.

"I was always happy enough with my local Belfast scene, working, doing the gigs."

She added: "It's now or never. I feel like you're not going to be young forever.

"Like, why not immortalise this on television forever while we're still gorge?"

Drag Race UK starts at 21:00 BST on Thursday 3 September

So what can fans expect from this series?

Mandi says "a good bit of drama" and a "gorgeous cast of high-personality divas".

"You're not ready for it, " she said. "This is going to be one for the books."

So is it sink or swim for Coral-Hole? Will she wear the crown and get the coveted £25,000 cash prize or sashay away?

Mirandi thinks she is going to do "just fine".

"The Irish, we know how to charm. We have charisma for days, and RuPaul loves the Irish," she said.

Drag Race UK starts at 21:00 BST on Thursday 3 September on BBC Three and is available to watch on BBC iPlayer.

articles.title: The chilling drama that will make you side with a female serial killer
articles.excerpt: Described as a drama for the ‘post-Epstein world’, Furious inverts true crime’s dead-girl trope, allowing women to be messy and monstrous
articles.content:
Described as a drama for the ‘post-Epstein world’, Furious inverts true crime’s dead-girl trope, allowing women to be messy and monstrous

5/5

Contains spoilers

Contains spoilers

It is difficult to think of a TV thriller darker and more transgressive than Furious, in which we are asked to empathise with a female serial killer who injects men with fentanyl and, enraptured, stays to watch their long, painful deaths. Catherine, played by 30-year-old Irish actress Lola Petticrew, keeps syringes in a tin bedazzled with plastic rhinestones, carries a bright sequinned bag and doodles pink hearts around the photographs of her next male victim.

Catherine presents like a child, and in a way, she still is one: psychologically suspended at the age she got trafficked into a paedophile ring, where she was starved, drugged, hit and raped on camera. The problem is her “memory sucks… because I got strangled so much”, so she uses an old photograph from that time to track down all the men she thinks may have hurt her, as well as find out what happened to her best friend Isabel – who died after giving birth aged 15.

The New Yorker described Furious – the season finale of which is now streaming on Disney+ – as a crime drama for the “post-Epstein world”, and although Elizabeth Meriwether (creator of The Dropout and sitcom New Girl) loosely based the show on the 1987 film Black Widow, its portrayal of sex trafficking so closely mirrors the details of Jeffrey Epstein’s convictions that at times Furious feels adapted from the pages of a newspaper.

The trafficking operation’s ringleader Jay Easton is an old, decrepit billionaire in cahoots with the FBI and cared for by his daughter, Emma, who – like Ghislaine Maxwell – dutifully arranges the delivery of underage girls like lambs to the slaughter. Far more horrifying than any of Catherine’s murders is the brief scene in which we watch Emma gently close the door on her wheelchair-bound father sitting opposite a blank-faced girl, casually telling him to “call me when you’re done”.

Some viewers might assume a show written by a woman featuring a female killer and all-male victims could be misandrist. Furious is feminist, yes, but not in a hectoring way. It remains subversive, entertaining and even funny during its bleakest moments, with prestige acting and cliché-free dialogue that breathes new life into the tired old police procedural. Running concurrently to Catherine’s killings is the abrasive friendship between NYPD-detective-turned-new-FBI-agent Alice, played by a mesmerising Emmy Rossum, and her spunky boss, Nora (Quincy Tyler Bernstine), who has some of the best lines in the genre.

Nora, a jaded drunk, thinks newbie Alice is too soft. But they are both motivated by buried grievances: for Nora, a historic sex-trafficking case that got away from her, and Alice by her own abusive past. In one of this year’s greatest TV twists, we see Alice’s colleague and love interest Danny (Scoot McNairy) – the show’s one and only good guy – open up Jay Easton’s hard drive of child-abuse videos to find one titled “Alice”. He glimpses just a second, but it’s enough to stop him getting into bed with her even when she needs him most. “I just can’t get your face from the video out of my head,” he says, with a sadness that lands like a lump in your throat.

While Catherine’s trauma is horribly simple, Alice’s is more complicated – and Rossum masterfully delivers one of the most daring and complicated depictions of trauma and PTSD ever seen on screen. Alice’s ex-boyfriend is fellow fed Marshall (an unsettling Jake Lacy), who used to beat Alice so badly he put her in hospital. The way he pulled her out of the shower to hit her means she now avoids washing for days. But, as can sometimes happen with trauma, the brain has warped the line between abuse and desire, so Alice uses an app for sex so rough she turns up to work with a busted lip.

This is a storyline only a talent such as Meriwether – a writer who so boldly interrogated female desire in last year’s astonishing Dying for Sex, starring Michelle Williams as a terminally ill woman who leaves her husband to embark on a sexual odyssey – could pull off. It also takes a talent such as Meriwether to have given disabled actor and comedian Steve Way the unusual opportunity to “fall in love” on screen, while also giving him one of the funniest TV scenes of the year, in which he mischievously uses his motorised wheelchair to keep evading detectives.

Most transgressive of all is how Furious justifies vengeance. Alice’s own destructive impulses eventually catch up with Catherine’s, the pair forming an alliance despite the fact that one is chasing the other. Both, ultimately, want Jay Easton punished, and Catherine senses there is more than professional duty motivating Alice’s quest for justice. “Have you ever killed someone?” Catherine asks her softly in the season finale. “It’s power, watching someone die. There’s this moment watching someone go where you’re not scared at all. And I was always scared.”

Alice finally finds her power when, after following Catherine to Jay Easton’s house, she is able to take revenge against him. Again, we are asked to empathise with such actions, as Easton tells Alice that her video was one of his favourites. “You’re the movie star!” he says, his eyes shining with grotesque joy.

Back in the office, Nora – brutally unsentimental, in a way we rarely see from women on screen – commands her to watch the video. If you want this job, you have to “face it”, she says. In a scene that most viewers will find hard to forget, we see Alice sit in front of the computer and watch what was done to her, before realising the video has been shared and downloaded more than 50,000 times. Furious has been renewed for season two, and you get the sense a furious Alice may pick up from where the now-imprisoned Catherine left off.

From Making a Murderer and Gone Girls to Broadchurch, Top of the Lake and The Ted Bundy Tapes, television is littered with dead girls and women who no longer have a voice, with true-crime docs and dramas endlessly psychoanalysing the motives of men. For all its horrors, Furious offers some rare mercies: its allows women to be messy and monstrous; and, crucially, to survive.

Season one of Furious is streaming on Disney+

articles.title: Trump says US position on Falklands 'one of many' under review
articles.excerpt: The UK says Falkland islanders "are British with a right to determine their own future".
articles.content:
• Published
    1 September 2026

Donald Trump has said the United States' position on the Falkland Islands is "one of many" under review, as he pressed the UK to increase military spending.

The US president said the UK has "got some problems, but they'll get solved" when asked about defence funding as a follow-up question to his response on the Falklands.

It comes after The Daily Telegraph reported, external US defence officials were drawing up proposals to incentivise Nato allies to meet their spending pledges, with a threat to oppose UK sovereignty over the Falklands among the possible options.

The UK government responded by saying Falkland islanders "are British with a right to determine their own future".

A spokesperson added: "The islanders have repeatedly expressed their wish to remain a British overseas territory and our commitment to them is unwavering."

The Falkland Islands, in the south-west Atlantic Ocean, remain the subject of a sovereignty dispute between Britain and Argentina.

The two countries waged a brief but bitter war over the territory in 1982. A British military task force ejected Argentine forces, which had landed on the Falklands to stake a territorial claim.

The 74-day conflict led to the deaths of 255 British military personnel, three islanders and 649 Argentine military personnel.

Previous US administrations have formally recognised the UK's de facto administration of the islands, but have not taken a formal position regarding sovereignty.

Speaking to reporters on Monday, Trump was asked by the BBC if he was reviewing the US position on the Falkland Islands.

The president replied: "I always review every position. That's just one of many."

Trump's remarks were labelled "nonsense" by Labour MP Dame Emily Thornberry, who chairs the Commons foreign affairs committee, as she asked the UK government to issue an official response in the House of Commons.

Foreign Office Minister Uma Kumaran replied: "The UK has no doubt about its sovereignty over the Falkland Islands.

"They are and will always remain a British overseas territory in line with the wishes of the Falkland islanders.

"The UK is steadfast in our support for the islanders' rights of self-determination."

Kumaran said she had seen Trump's comments, adding: "Our position remains unchanged."

Defence spending pledges

In April, an internal Pentagon email reported by Reuters suggested the US was considering options to punish Nato allies it believed had failed to support its war in Iran.

The options reportedly included the prospect of the US reviewing its position on Britain's claim to the Falklands.

Reports of this proposal have re-emerged in recent days in relation to defence spending.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he will honour a commitment made by predecessor Sir Keir Starmer to devote 3.5% of UK gross domestic product (GDP) on core defence spending by 2035.

On Tuesday, Chancellor John Healey told The Times, external he would "set out a clear path" to meeting that Nato pledge at the next government spending review, expected in the spring of next year.

He added that this would also include a target date for increasing spending to 3% of GDP.

Healey resigned as defence secretary in Sir Keir Starmer's government following a row over military spending.

His resignation letter in June expressed his frustration that the government had no clear timetable to hit the 3% spending target, which he believed should happen by 2030.

Chagos deal questions

The UK government has also faced questions over whether it will continue with a deal to hand over the Chagos Islands to Mauritius and pay to lease back the joint US-UK military base on Diego Garcia.

It was confirmed in April that the deal had been paused indefinitely because of Trump pulling his support.

Kumaran told MPs on Tuesday that "maintaining long-term operational control and security of the base remains a top priority and is the entire basis for the UK-Mauritius agreement."

The minister also said funding for the treaty would be provided for "within the existing spending review settlements" for the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office and the Ministry of Defence.

Conservative shadow defence secretary James Cartlidge criticised the remarks and said the deal "belongs on the ash heap of history".

He said in a statement: "Burnham should show some backbone and break with this terrible legacy of the Starmer years by ditching his crazy Chagos deal once and for all, and spending the savings on our armed forces."

In the Commons, Conservative shadow Foreign Office minister Wendy Morton noted Sir Keir's administration acknowledged in April that the Chagos treaty had become "impossible to agree at political level" and asked what had changed.

Kumaran said the Burnham government would "continue to work with the US and Mauritius to find a way forward that is in the UK's best interests and protects our national security".

articles.title: Halloween The Game: Review: Scary, Fun, And A Bit Janky
articles.excerpt: Hunting, stalking, scaring and then butchering your friends has never been more fun
articles.content:
HalloweenHalloween: The GameIllFonic

I’ve played a lot of asymmetrical horror games, including Predator: Hunting Grounds, Friday the 13th, Killer Klowns From Outer Space (remember that one?), and Dead by Daylight. For the most part, I’ve not really enjoyed them. So I wasn’t sure what to expect with the latest one of “those” games, Halloween: The Game. To my surprise, this is an asymmetrical horror game that I’m really digging, even if I’m also having to put up with some jank.

If you’re even slightly familiar with these kinds of games and horror movies, you probably don’t even need to see a single frame of gameplay to guess the basic setup for Halloween. One person is the masked killer Michael Myers, and up to four other people take on the role of survivors trying to, well, survive Michael’s killing spree. As in many other similar online horror games, Michael has access to abilities and powers that let him get around the map quickly. He is also immortal. You can damage him and even stop him temporarily, but your main goal is to escape alive.

The big difference with Halloween: The Game is that each match is filled with multiple NPCs, some based on characters from the original films and others that are more generic townspeople. These NPC characters really make playing Halloween a treat, even if you only have one other person to play with.

As Michael, you always have many targets to stalk and kill however you see fit, beyond just a few of your buddies trying to escape.  And if you’re playing as survivors, you have a choice: Help as many townsfolk as you can to escape, or leave them to die. Helping them gets you more XP, which is helpful for unlocking better starting gear and other benefits. But every moment you stick around on the map helping people hide or call the police is giving the Michael player more time to find you and stab a kitchen knife into your skull.

Having NPCs chilling around town, cleaning or watching TV or smoking a cigarette on the porch, adds so much to each match. The various maps, each a different size, feel more alive, and exploring them feels more exciting.

As Michael, you have more targets to stalk, hunt, and kill. And as the survivors, you have some breathing room between you and Michael. But each time he kills one of them, the game lets you know. And sometimes, if he’s close, you can hear the kill, which is genuinely scary if you’re alone in a house looking for some supplies to help you make your escape.

Murdering and scaring your friends

I have so many memorable little stories to tell from playing this game with others. At one point, someone I was playing with entered a house, locked the door behind them, and then entered a bedroom to talk to an NPC townsperson to convince them to follow them to a possible escape.

I watched all of this because I was using Michael’s shadowy ghost ability, which lets the killer invisibly fly around the map and even move through doors that aren’t lit up. The one catch is you can’t materialize in direct view of someone or in light. Thankfully, the room they were in had a closet. I ghosted my way to that closet, materialized inside, and then popped out. I was in a voice party with the person and heard them scream, then jump out a window through the glass to escape, leaving the poor NPC to her fate. I laughed a lot as I stabbed her. (Nobody take that last bit out of context.)

Michael is genuinely a force to be reckoned with in the game and is scary as heck. Once you’ve figured out his abilities and limitations, being him is a blast as you feel incredibly powerful. Just walking around a corner to surprise a friend and make them yelp in fear and turn around is so much fun. And the game rewards Michael players for stalking victims before killing them, giving you bonus XP for taking them out when they’re scared. So screwing with your friends by turning off the power or breaking a window near them and then vanishing isn’t just fun, it’s encouraged!

Playing against him is also exciting and terrifying. The game gives you enough tools to keep him from just walking over you all in minutes. Flashlights, guns, bikes, and even some weird magical items that feel a bit out of place help the survivors have a chance of holding Michael back while they collect parts to escape via a car, basement, or some other exit. Wait around long enough, and as the bodies pile up and the police arrive, you might be able to escape via a police wagon. And if you can get a few townies out of danger, all the better, as you get more XP and deny the Michael player the thrill of the kill and their own chance at extra XP.

But good luck sticking to your plan the moment Michael appears out of nowhere behind a door and you have to quickly escape or else get your head slammed into a television set.

Bugs and meh solo mode

Unfortunately, in my time with Halloween, I encountered numerous bugs and jank that at times killed matches. Some of these were funny, like NPC townspeople sometimes getting stuck on top of roofs that are normally inaccessible.

Other times they were frustrating, like being unable to attack or kill people as Michael because I’d picked up an object or weapon too close to a wall or in the middle of an animation. Executions, which are often violent and graphic in a classic slasher-movie style, can also look janky from time to time. And I wish the game made it easier for friends to get back into the match after death. In our matches, it only happened once, with a dead player returning as a cop. I’m not sure if we’re just bad at the game or something isn’t working as intended.

The developer says that some of the janky issues and bugs I experienced will be fixed with a day-one patch, and the studio also plans to support the game with post-launch updates. But not all of the issues I encountered, like performance problems and crashes, were included in the list of things to be fixed. Hopefully these issues are worked out by launch or soon after, because when Halloween: The Game was working, I was having a blast. And with October coming, I’m excited to get a group of pals together and take turns killing each other.

One last thing: Halloween: The Game does include a single-player story mode in which you play as Michael Myers and recreate many of the events seen in the original film. The attention to detail in these missions is great, but there aren’t many of them; they aren’t particularly fun to play, and function more as a neat tutorial.

If you were planning to buy this game because of the advertised solo mode and don’t have any friends interested in playing this with you (or you just don’t enjoy playing online PvP games), I wouldn’t pick up Halloween. While you can play as Michael against bots outside of the campaign, it isn’t as fun as playing with others mixed in.

A so-so single-player mode and some jankiness weren’t enough to keep me away from Halloween: The Game. I’ve already sunk nearly a dozen hours into it, leveling up both my survivors and Michael and unlocking new cosmetics and abilities. The vibes of Halloween are so strong, complete with the film’s iconic music. And when it all comes together and works, it is truly a blast with some pals.

Halloween just needs a few updates and fixes, which hopefully will come soon after it launches on PS5, Xbox, and PC on September 4 via paid early access. Halloween: The Game launches for everyone else on September 8.

articles.title: Trump threatens more strikes as death toll in Iran rises to 18
articles.excerpt: Trump says US can hit Iran ‘anytime we want’ as Tehran says deadly strikes, including on wedding party, a war crime.
articles.content:
Trump says US can hit Iran ‘anytime we want’ as Tehran says deadly strikes, including on wedding party, a war crime.

Trump says US sees ‘everything’ Iran does, threatens further attacks

United States President Donald Trump has threatened more attacks on Iran, warning that Washington could hit Iran “anytime we want”, as the death toll from the latest US strikes climbed to 18, with at least 108 others wounded.

Trump’s threat on Wednesday came after the US and Iran exchanged their biggest barrage since July. The US military struck cities and areas along Iran’s southern coast, near the blockaded Strait of Hormuz, including a wedding party in the city of Kuhestak.

Recommended Stories

  • list 1 of 4Republican senator calls on Trump to fire Secretary of Defence Hegseth
  • list 2 of 4Israeli PM says Israel is working to overthrow Iran’s government
  • list 3 of 4The long-term implications of Pete Hegseth’s US military purges
  • list 4 of 4Trump suggests renaming Strait of Hormuz as Trump Strait amid Iran war

Iran retaliated with attacks on US bases across the Middle East, including Bahrain, Iraq and Jordan.

Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump said, “We hit them very hard last night” and that the strikes “took out all of the new equipment that they tried to build along the Strait of Hormuz”.

“It was a very heavy attack last night. And we’re prepared to do another one. And anytime we want,” he said.

Iranian officials said at least 18 people were killed in the US strikes.

The victims included two children, according to Mohammad-Reza Zafarghandi, Iran’s health minister. One of them was a four-year-old who was killed in the strike on the wedding party in Kuhestak in Sirik county.

At least four people were killed in that strike.

Esmaeil Baghaei, the spokesman for Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, described the Kuhestak attack as a “war crime” and hit back at US claims that it does not target civilians.

“The reality is so horrifying that even American propaganda has never dared make the claim [the US military] is making today. Sirik is not a story. The civilians are real. The victims are real”, Baghaei wrote on X.

Iranian media said the funeral for the four Kuhestak victims will be held on Thursday.

‘Uncomfortable strategic position’

The six-month war has led to a spike in oil prices, roiled the global economy and posed increasing political problems for Trump’s Republican Party ahead of November midterm elections in the US.

Only 31 percent of Americans approve of the war, while some 63 percent disapprove, according to a poll by the Reuters news agency and the Ipsos polling firm in August. Voters are particularly unhappy about high gas prices. Since the fighting resumed this weekend, the price of Brent crude oil, the international standard, has climbed to about $95, up more than 30 percent from the start of the war.

Trump’s approval rating has also fallen from 40 percent to 33 percent since the conflict began, according to Reuters/Ipsos polling.

On Wednesday, Trump said he did not think the renewed military campaign ⁠would last long. He also reiterated his position that the upcoming elections were not a factor in his Iran strategy.

“Number one, I’m not running. My party is running, and I’m going to help my party,” he told reporters in the Oval Office. “But I think my party respects the fact that we’re not allowing Iran to have a nuclear weapon.”

Iran has denied seeking a nuclear weapon.

Tariq Khan, a retired Pakistani lieutenant-general and former commander of the Pakistan Army’s Frontier Corps, said the US “now finds itself in an increasingly uncomfortable strategic position in the Iran war”.

“The US has not succeeded in restoring the maritime environment that existed before the war, and is now expending military resources to deal with a problem the war itself helped create,” he told Al Jazeera, referring to Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

The strait was a free-flowing international waterway carrying roughly one-fifth of the world’s traded oil before the war. Tehran shut the waterway in response to the US and Israeli strikes on February 18 that began the war. Despite repeated US claims that the strait remains open, only a handful of vessels now pass through each day, and Iran continues to target ships attempting the crossing.

On Wednesday, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said two oil tankers had struck mines and were disabled while attempting an unauthorised transit. Separately, Saudi shipping firm Bahri reported that two Filipino sailors were killed in an attack on their vessel earlier in the week.

Iran’s Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA), which Tehran set up to police the Strait of Hormuz, added 11 more ships to its blacklist for alleged “noncompliance” this week, on top of the 45 blacklisted last week. The PGSA said the vessels will face fines, seizures or confiscation unless they submit required documentation to Iran before attempting to cross the strait.

Strait of Hormuz

At the same time, the US has intensified an economic isolation campaign against Iran, threatening to slap countries that ‌trade with Tehran with massive sanctions, while also maintaining its own blockade in the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump on Wednesday continued to insist that Washington was in control of the strait, saying US forces were helping bring “lots of boats out every day with millions of barrels of oil”.

“We are, for the most part, doing it without trouble. Every once in a while they shoot a drone, and we knock it down. We have control, very strong control,” he said.

On Tuesday, he had claimed the US Navy was helping escort some 30 ships out of the strait every day. Before the war, some 130 ships transited the waterway daily.

Khan, the former Pakistani general, said Iran understands it cannot defeat the US conventionally and is seeking to make the war costly for Trump.

“If Trump escalates, Iran can portray America as being drawn deeper into another Middle Eastern war; if he restrains himself, Tehran can claim that American military superiority cannot compel Iran to surrender,” he said.

“Iran does not need a battlefield victory; it needs to remain standing, keep the economic disruption alive, and make the war politically costly for the US. Tehran has to make American victory increasingly unaffordable – militarily, economically and electorally.”

articles.title: The Michael J. Fox Foundation Releases "So Your Friend Has Parkinson's" Awareness Campaign for Parkinson's Research
