News provided by

Sep 02, 2026, 08:00 ET

  • Michael J. Fox and Harrison Ford partner to drive awareness of Parkinson's disease and The Michael J. Fox Foundation (MJFF)

  • Campaign written and directed by Ryan Reynolds' entertainment company, Maximum Effort, to bring attention to MJFF's mission to accelerate better treatments and a cure

NEW YORK, Sept. 2, 2026 /CNW/ -- As part of its commitment to accelerate Parkinson's research breakthroughs and unite a worldwide community of patients, scientists, the biopharmaceutical industry, government and philanthropists, The Michael J. Fox Foundation (MJFF) today releases its latest brand awareness campaign, "So…Your Friend Has Parkinson's." The campaign will appear across social media, digital channels, CTV and broadcast television. Watch the full video on YouTube here.

The Foundation partnered with entertainment company Maximum Effort, helmed by MJFF Board member Ryan Reynolds, to bring the tremendous momentum of today's Parkinson's research to broad audiences through a gently humorous, accessible and compelling message. 

The campaign features Michael J. Fox and Harrison Ford in a playful exchange about how best to support a friend with Parkinson's, now the world's fastest-growing neurodegenerative disease, for which there is still no cure. Already impacting more than 6 million individuals worldwide, Parkinson's is projected to double globally by 2040. 

"The world has taken notice of the special relationship between Michael and Harrison. Our brand campaign combines humor and compassion to highlight the very serious purpose behind our work," said Debi Brooks, MJFF's CEO and Co-Founder. "It has been a joy to see these Hollywood giants come together to capture attention and channel it toward what matters most: bringing greater awareness and support to people and families living with Parkinson's." 

Fox and Ford's lighthearted banter uses humor to surface some of the real challenges of living with the disease, from changes in handwriting to social isolation. The nearly two-minute video -- also available at michaeljfox.org/BeAFriend -- exemplifies the signature optimism and candor Fox has brought to MJFF's mission to speed a cure, a mission now backed by more than $3 billion in Foundation-funded research globally. 

"Michael has a remarkable way of making difficult things easier to talk about, and that's part of what makes working with him and being his friend so special. We wanted to bring some of that honesty and humor to a conversation that a lot of people may not know how to have," said Harrison Ford. "Parkinson's affects millions of people, and sometimes the best thing you can do is simply be there. I'm glad we can use this campaign to help people feel a little more comfortable having those conversations, and to support the important work of The Michael J. Fox Foundation." 

Parkinson's research is at an extraordinary inflection point, with the potential for unprecedented scientific breakthroughs. Since its launch in 2000, the Foundation has relentlessly focused on galvanizing philanthropic resources to transform the state of Parkinson's drug development, helping drive the field to this moment of tremendous promise. The campaign leverages this momentum in advance of the public launch of MJFF's All Grit. No Quit. Campaign, a multi-year $2.5-billion fundraising initiative to further accelerate the development of new treatments, and ultimately, a cure.

"So…Your Friend Has Parkinson's" plays off the chemistry between Fox and Ford in Apple TV's Emmy-nominated original series "Shrinking." In the series, they portray characters living with Parkinson's, bringing to the screen -- and the national conversation -- many of the realities experienced by people and families living with the disease. Two members of MJFF's Patient Council serve as advisors to the "Shrinking" writers' room.

"The idea came from watching Harrison and Michael together on Shrinking. They have this incredible natural chemistry, and we wanted to see what happened if we took away the characters and just let them be themselves. So we gave them a question a lot of us will probably face at some point, but no one really knows how to answer: what do you do when a friend tells you they have Parkinson's?" said Kathleen Swanson, Head of Creative for Brand & Entertainment Marketing at Maximum Effort. "Harrison asks the honest questions. Michael answers them with his trademark humor and candor. And between the two of them, they somehow make a pretty difficult conversation feel remarkably easy. Hopefully we made something that's funny, useful, and makes it a little easier to show up for someone you love. Which, as it turns out, is mostly about showing up."

About The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research (MJFF)
As the world's largest nonprofit funder of Parkinson's research, The Michael J. Fox Foundation is dedicated to accelerating a cure for Parkinson's disease and improved therapies for those living with the condition today. The Foundation pursues its goals through an aggressively funded, highly targeted research program coupled with active global engagement of scientists, Parkinson's patients, business leaders, clinical trial participants, donors, and volunteers. In addition to funding $3 billion in research to date, the Foundation has fundamentally altered the trajectory of progress toward a cure. Operating at the hub of worldwide Parkinson's research, MJFF forges groundbreaking collaborations, creates robust open-access data sets and biosample libraries with its landmark clinical study (PPMI), increases the flow of participants into Parkinson's disease clinical trials with its online tool (Fox Trial Finder), promotes Parkinson's awareness, and coordinates the grassroots involvement of thousands of Team Fox members around the world. For more information, visit us at www.michaeljfox.org, Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn.

Maximum Effort makes movies, tv series, content, and cocktails for the personal amusement of Hollywood Star Ryan Reynolds. We occasionally share them with the general public. Producers of the Deadpool films, Free Guy, The Adam Project, and Welcome to Wrexham.

articles.title: 'We will never know what could have been' Liverpool midfielder bids emotional farewell and signals downfall of Klopp's Kids
articles.excerpt: Watching Liverpool's youngsters be loaned, sold and forgotten will, no doubt, be enjoyable for the club's Premier League peers
articles.content:
• Facebook
  • X
  • Pinterest
  • Email

As Jurgen Klopp’s swansong, he hoisted Liverpool into one final Premier League title race, finishing third behind Arsenal and Manchester City, and lifted the Carabao Cup.

The last trophy he brought back to Anfield came courtesy of ‘Klopp’s Kids’ — a unit of youngsters that took to the pitch in Wembley cameos and secured victory against Chelsea — and was, undoubtedly, one of the German’s finest feats as manager of the Reds.

Liverpool, back then, were different. Stefan Bajcetic drawing the curtain on an injury-plagued, but once highly-anticipated Reds career, proves it. And it could be a long journey back to the summit.

Bajcetic leaving Liverpool should remind fans how deep the rot spread under Arne Slot, and how much work rests on Andoni Iraola’s shoulders

'But he was injured! That’s nobody’s fault,' some might claim. But it isn’t Bajcetic’s departure in total isolation that should sting, it’s what his exit should remind Liverpool fans of. And that is the sheer number of developing talents that have been discarded, loaned, sold, and forgotten about since Klopp’s time on Merseyside.

From future club captain Trent Alexander-Arnold choosing Real Madrid — after the Reds lifted their first Premier League title in front of fans for 35 years, no less — to Harvey Elliot’s recent La Liga loan departure. After a torrid year at Aston Villa, the look on the Englishman’s face as he fielded questions from the Valencia media was… not pleasant to witness.

Young players once deemed to be Liverpool’s future, talents that the German was able to extract the very best from, have gone from a Carabao Cup-winning unit, and making reliable cameo appearances in both European competitions and the Premier League, to being spread around here, there and everywhere.

Instead, the Reds have spent big in their two previous transfer windows - their total expenditure on attackers alone exceeds £500 million - and lost the heart and soul that made Klopp’s reign so special, and so successful.

Is it a surprise that Slot was able to win a Premier League title? He inherited a team whose muscles and minds had been ruthlessly shaped by the German — one that also included a career-best and still-hungry Mohamed Salah — and rode that wave to English top-flight glory.

But, depressingly, the cost of that victory has likely set Liverpool back by years. To win it, Slot decided against using the German’s youngsters in any meaningful capacity, going full-throttle on extracting the last dregs of mentality and fitness that had been instilled in the core Reds by Klopp.

But a once wise decision — or at least one that felt wise, at the time — continued into the 2025-26 season, and questions surrounding Liverpool’s mentality quickly surfaced. When Reds legend Salah told the press last December that he felt he was being forced out of the club, tensions reached their boiling point.

If the club’s hierarchy could make an all-time superstar feel this way, an individual that had lifted Liverpool onto his shoulders and dragged them to the previous term’s Premier League-winning finish line, how was it making ‘Klopp’s Kids’ feel, behind the scenes?

Jarell Quansah? A lacklustre game to start the season versus Ipswich Town in 2024-25, and few opportunities after. Now, he’s at Bayer Leverkusen, and receiving England call-ups. Bobby Clark? He once ran riot for the Reds during their Europa League campaign in 2023-24. Now, he’s at Derby County, with three goal involvements in his first four Championship matches this term.

Jayden Danns? A scouser through-and-through, one who bagged twice versus Southampton in the FA Cup, no less, during Klopp’s swansong season. He’s back in the Liverpool Under-21s, and last appeared for the first team 12 months ago, again versus Southampton — for 15 minutes.

James McConnell? He’s in the Under-21s, too. And, finally, Bajcetic, who appeared in 27 games across the German’s final two seasons at the helm, even delivering a Man of the Match-worthy performance in 2023’s Merseyside derby at Anfield?

He’s gone, and wrote today on Instagram: “I never planned to write a goodbye message, because I was where I always wanted to be.

“I fought all the injuries and adversities with the motivation of paying back the love and trust you showed me… We will never know what could have been.”

And perhaps the Spaniard is a slightly different case — a talent thwarted by injuries, and dealt an unfair hand throughout his Premier League career.

But maybe seeing his fellow Carabao Cup-winning youngsters be loaned elsewhere, and denied first-team minutes, witnessing the standards drop on Merseyside, weaker training sessions, weaker performances, weaker mentality, weaker leadership, all in the aftermath of Klopp’s departure… perhaps that also played a role in Bajcetic’s recovery, or lack thereof.

Under the German, Liverpool became a family. Under his successor, that family became estranged. Can Iraola turn back the clock? That remains to be seen, but the damage cannot be reversed. As the saying goes, it’s all up from here — but is it? Let's hope so.

Kedar Bayley is a trained journalist specialising in culture reporting. As a fan of Liverpool FC, he writes on the Reds often. Knowledgable about all things sports, cinema and television, you can find his words in Screen International, FourFourTwo, Manchester Evening News and more.

articles.title: Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9B - KitGuru
articles.excerpt: Nvidia is making another major acquisition. This week, the company announced plans to acquire the Hugging Face platform, which has gone on to be used by millions of AI projects around the world.
articles.content:
Matthew Wilson 17 mins ago Featured Announcement, General Tech

Nvidia is making another major acquisition. This week, the company announced plans to acquire the Hugging Face platform, which has gone on to be used by millions of AI projects around the world.

The deal will see Nvidia buying Hugging Face for a price of $12,930,300,000. Currently, Hugging Face is home to millions of AI models, hundreds of thousands of datasets and more than one-million apps. The platform has over 18 million registered developers, and is used by more than 200,000 companies.

After the acquisition, Nvidia says Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the AI ecosystem. Developers will still choose the models they want, the frameworks they want, the clouds and inference service providers they want and the computing platforms they want. NVIDIA compute will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face.

Nvidia is already one of Hugging Face’s largest contributors, with more than 500 models and over 250 datasets published on the platform. The company says the acquisition will allow Hugging Face to operate at greater scale, improving reliability, safety and model evaluation while maintaining the open ecosystem that has made the service widely adopted across the AI community.

articles.title: Minimum wage shame list reveals Scottish firms that failed to pay staff
articles.excerpt: Three of the firms topping the list in Scotland - including North East bakers Murdoch Allan & Son - each owed more than £20,000 to underpaid workers.
articles.content:
Fifty firms in Scotland have been revealed on a UK government list naming and shaming employers that failed to pay staff minimum wage.

Three of the companies topping the list in Scotland - including North East bakers Murdoch Allan & Son - each owed more than £20,000 to underpaid workers.

The Department for Business said 658 employers across the UK have been ordered to repay £4m after more than 27,000 workers have been left out of pocket.

Nearly 700 workers were affected in Scotland.

The largest amount underpaid in Scotland was by family-owned nursery chain Collin Care Ltd in Glasgow, which owed £28,149 to 77 workers.

Next came bakers Murdoch Allan & Son in Peterhead, which failed to pay £24,150 to seven employees.

This was followed by Fiona Burgoyne trading as Horsechoice - a horse dealer and showjumping yard in Edinburgh - which underpaid four workers by £22,422.

Minimum wage rises to £12.71 an hour as firms warn of impact

Minimum wage: Who is getting a pay rise and how much is it?

Several other nurseries based in Glasgow featured on the list, including Victoria Park Kindergarten, Clarence Nursery and Acorn Park Nursery.

Dynamic Retail Ltd trading as Scotfresh in Dundee failed to pay £14,452 to 215 workers, while Aulds Delicious Desserts in Renfrew owed £9,435 to 89 staff.

Also on the list were Glasgow restaurants La Vita and The Butchershop Bar & Grill, which underpaid 66 workers by £5,440.

Two companies - Saash Foods Limited and KA Scotland Ltd - trading as fast food chain Pepe's, failed to pay £2,587 to two workers and £700 to 14 employees, respectively.

Businesses in hospitality, retail, construction and food production were all represented on the list.

'Technical breach' led to underpayment

Collin Care Ltd's financial director Douglas Collin said the statement related to a historical inquiry which spanned several years and only involved a particular section of its workforce.

He said the claim had been settled in full, more than a year ago and that "at no point did the company deliberately seek to underpay workers or avoid its legal obligations."

"It related to a technical breach of the classification of staff due to a time delay in getting completed paperwork from various training companies," he said.

"We voluntarily worked with HMRC for over two years and supplied all information and paperwork requested.

"Any underpayment is calculated at the date of payment and not at the time of the error, so this resulted in an inflated figure."

He added that within days of HMRC finalising its inquiry and sending the company its calculations, every member (or ex-member) of staff was paid in full, along with a large penalty to HMRC.

"Collin Care Ltd are, and have been, a Real Living Wage employer for several years, we have taken corrective action and do not envisage this situation ever arising again," he added.

What are the national living wage and national minimum wage?

About 2.7 million people in the UK received a pay rise in April as the national living wage went up by 50p to £12.71 for over 21s.

Workers aged 18-20 saw an 85p increase in national minimum wage to £10.85 and under 18s and apprentices got 45p more to £8 an hour.

For someone working full time, national living wage amounts to £24,784.50 a year.

Some workers do not qualify for either the national minimum wage or national living wage.

This includes people who are self-employed, company directors, volunteers, members of the armed forces and prisoners.

It is a criminal offence for employers not to pay the correct national minimum and living wages to eligible employees.

The rates apply even if workers are not paid by the hour.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said: "The best businesses know that looking after your workers isn't just the right thing to do, it's the smart thing to do.

"Most employers already understand this, and I want to work with them to ensure they have every piece of guidance and support available to help them follow the rules.

"Short-changing your staff isn't a shortcut to success and we are determined to stamp it out."

articles.title: Arsenal analysed: 5 reasons we were victorious at Villa
articles.excerpt: Adrian Clarke dissects our success at Aston Villa
articles.content:
Bukayo Saka's goal was all we needed to secure three points against Aston Villa at Villa Park.

The number 7 bagged his second in as many games to keep our season perfect so far, but how did we overcome Unai Emery's side?

Adrian Clarke has dived into the detail to unearth five reasons why our trip to the Midlands was a successful one.

KEEPING THE DOOR SHUT 

This was yet another impressive defensive lockdown from Mikel Arteta’s well-oiled defensive machine.  

Limiting the hosts to very little in terms of goalmouth action, this was the first time Aston Villa had failed to register a shot on target at home in the Premier League since 2016.  

The only minor success the home side had was in the wide areas, especially when switching play from right to left, but down the spine of the pitch they made no headway whatsoever.  

We were compact out of possession with Declan Rice often the deepest midfielder, occasionally taking up positions alongside the centre backs.  

This 5-4-1 out-of-possession shape was used for around 20 per cent of the contest, and clearly highlights how Rice dropped in… 

Towards the end of the match, when Mikel Merino replaced Martin Odegaard as our number 10, we tweaked our off-the-ball shape to good effect.  

Trying not to sit too deep, opting to press with a little more force, we saw Merino and Havertz lead a 4-2-2-2 formation for the closing stages.

While we were comfortable dealing with Villa’s forays forward, on the rare occasion when a gap opened up, it was notable how quickly we regrouped as a side.  

Working incredibly hard, we ensured the door was never left open for Aston Villa to trouble David Raya.  

MATCH WINNING MOVEMENT  

The only goal of the game owed so much to clever, forceful off-the-ball movement by Riccardo Calafiori and Bukayo Saka.  

It was not easy to break down a well-organised mid-block from Villa, but one moment of collective excellence helped us take the lead.  

Initially, Calafiori was blocking the path for Christhian Mosquera to pass to Eberechi Eze, but the bright Italian was smart enough to realise that if he spun into a different space, the area would open up nicely.

By moving himself behind his marker, while staying on the inside, our rampaging left back allowed Mosquera to find Eze, while simultaneously offering himself to our No.10, who slipped a lovely pass to him beyond the last line.   

Please also note (below) how early Bukayo Saka makes his darting run, sensing an opportunity to score… 

Calafiori then produced a perfect low cross on the slide for Saka, who cleverly changed the angle of his run to cut across Ian Maatsen’s path.  

This allowed Saka to get to the ball first, netting his second goal of the campaign.  

It was great play which was indebted to the brightness of those two players’ movement.  

WONDERFUL WORK RATE  

We ran an incredible 123.2km at Villa Park, the longest distance recorded by any side across the first 20 games of the new campaign.  

Incessant in our running, on and off the ball, it superseded an impressive distance covered of 119.8km against Coventry City on the opening night.

In the context of this match in isolation, we certainly proved that we had superior athleticism.  

As outlined in the table below, we significantly topped Villa’s running stats in all departments.

Individually, Kai Havertz led the way. In footballing terms, it was a difficult evening for the German striker, but his effort levels remained high throughout.  

Always moving in search of the ball, and determined to press with ferocity, Havertz could not have worked any harder.  

His 12.3km shift, coupled with 25 sprints (the third most by any player in a game so far) saw the front man run with more intensity than any other striker has managed this term.  

MAGNIFICENT RICE

Our central midfield unit purred all game long, dominating their opposite numbers at Villa Park.  

All three starters, Declan Rice, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Odegaard, helped us take a firm grip of a game which was largely played out between both penalty boxes.  

Rice delivered a wonderful individual display, especially in the second half when his determination leapt off the page.  

This block & tackle combination (below), occurring within four seconds of each other in the second half, showcased how vital the England international is when we are defending a lead.  

Sprinting eight yards to throw himself in front of a Ross Barkley shot, Rice tumbled to the ground before instantly picking himself up to win a key tackle against Emi Buendia… 

That was one of several defensive highlights. Before leaving the field late on, Rice’s numbers read;   

  • Passes: 77 
  • Passes in Final Third: 20 
  • Pass Accuracy: 92.2% 
  • Tackles: 3 
  • Interceptions: 1 
  • Ball Recoveries: 7 
  • Chances Created: 2 

SUPER SUBS

Mikel Merino and debutant Bruno Guimaraes both played outstandingly well after being introduced in the 71st minute.  

World Cup winner Merino held onto the ball wonderfully well under pressure, completing all 14 of his passes and all three of his dribbles. Winning six of eight duels too, the Spaniard was very strong.  

Those qualities calmed us down, took us further up the pitch and eased some pressure. Below is a map of Merino's passes, defensive work and dribbles during his crucial cameo.

On his Premier League debut for the Gunners, Guimaraes also sparkled, thanks to some fine defensive work and a willingness to show attacking ambition. 

Looking very nimble and classy, the Brazil international was first to several 50-50s, and this slide rule pass to release Havertz for a 1v1 was top class.  

In and out of possession, Guimaraes has built a reputation for being one of the most effective all-round central midfielders in the game.  

And this brief but confident cameo gave us reasons to feel very optimistic about his potential influence this season.  

Guimaraes and Merino improved the engine room at just the right moment at Villa Park.

Saka earns Arsenal hard-fought win at Aston Villa

Bukayo Saka scored the only goal as Premier League champions Arsenal came away from Aston Villa with all three points.

The England international slid the ball into a near-empty net from Riccardo Calafiori's cutback, with what was the first shot on target.

Villa went close in the first half when Emiliano Buendia's shot hit the crossbar, although a goal may well have been disallowed for a foul had the ball found the net.

Not long before Arsenal's goal, they were awarded a penalty for an Ian Maatsen foul on Saka, but a video assistant referee review found the incident happened outside the box so it was overturned and a free-kick awarded instead.

Kai Havertz forced a save from Villa's debutant goalkeeper Zion Suzuki as the Gunners tried to make the win safe.

Arsenal sent on England defender Ezri Konsa for a second-half debut against his former club, and he received a good reaction from Villa fans 10 days after his departure.

Mikel Arteta's Arsenal move to six points with their win, while it is back-to-back defeats for Aston Villa, who have lost a large chunk of last season's team.

Aston Villa analysis: New-look team need time

Aston Villa vs Arsenal: Unai Emery post-match interview

Unai Emery is having to build a Villa 2.0 after a summer in which he has lost almost the entire spine of his Europa League-winning team.

A narrow home defeat by the champions will not have been as alarming as the 4-0 loss at Brighton on the opening day.

But this was the first time Villa failed to have a shot on target in a home Premier League game since May 2016 against Newcastle United under caretaker boss Eric Black – when they had already been relegated.

In fact, they are the first team to not have a shot on target after two Premier League games since Swansea City in 2017-18.

There were debuts for Japan goalkeeper Suzuki and ex-Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson – replacements for the departed Emiliano Martinez and Ollie Watkins.

Suzuki showed both good and bad sides – going for a corner and missing it early on and later spilling a Havertz shot which he gathered at the second attempt.

He also made saves from a Rice header and a Havertz one-on-one chance. On both occasions there was an offence - a foul and offside respectively - but Suzuki still made the stops to be sure.

He also looked confident and comfortable with passing the ball at the back.

Jackson did not have a lot of joy on his Villa bow up front – but Watkins would also have struggled to do anything with little service.

The closest they went was when Buendia crashed his long-range effort off the woodwork, but there had been a tackle just before it that would probably have ruled out a goal, had it come.

Summer signings Alejandro Garnacho and Aaron Wan-Bissaka both came on in the second half for their Villa Park debuts.

Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis were both watching from the stands at Villa Park and are expected to finalise moves on Tuesday's deadline day.

At 1,911 pieces, the Lego Sony PlayStation is smaller than the Lego Atari 2600 (2,532 pieces) and Lego Nintendo Entertainment System (2,646 pieces), but larger than the Lego Sega Genesis (480 pieces). All of Lego's video game console sets have had varied extras, including a retro TV set for the Lego NES and multiple cartridges for the Lego 2600.

articles.title: Invasive tropical mosquito found breeding in east London
articles.excerpt: Climate crisis could increase incursions of Aedes aegypti, which can transmit Zika virus and dengue, experts say
articles.content:
Climate crisis could increase incursions of Aedes aegypti, which can transmit Zika virus and dengue, experts say

An mosquito capable of transmitting tropical diseases has been found breeding in homes in east London, with experts warning that the rapidly warming climate will lead to greater “incursions of invasive mosquitoes”.

This is the first time the species has been identified breeding in the UK and the fourth time it has been detected.

Aedes aegypti, which are normally found in tropical and subtropical regions, can transmit dengue, chikungunya and Zika virus in countries where these infections are circulating. While these diseases are rarely deadly, they can cause complications, with Zika linked to serious problems during and after pregnancy.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said the risk to the public was low, with no evidence that the mosquitoes in east London have have caused human infections.

The initial finding was reported through UKHSA’s mosquito watch surveillance scheme. The agency said the species could have come into the UK in vehicles, baggage and imported plants and, if the insects found a suitable climate, they could survive.

It said that despite evidence of breeding, the species was not established in the UK and could not survive for long in the typical UK climate, which was too cold.

However, the agency warned that in a warming climate, “we will continue to see incursions of invasive mosquitoes, and increased reports of them being able to survive in the UK”.

David Smith, the advocacy and social change manager at the charity Buglife, said the rapidly warming climate was creating conditions that were more favourable for exotic and potentially invasive species to establish in the UK.

A study earlier this year found that chikungunya, an excruciating tropical disease, can now be transmitted in most of Europe because of higher temperatures caused by the climate crisis. The analysis was the first to assess the effect of temperature on the incubation time of the virus in the Asian tiger mosquito.

Smith said: “Recent reports of non-native invertebrates, including mosquito species, highlight the urgent need for the government to strengthen biosecurity, improve surveillance and address pathways such as the movement of potted plants and soils, through which numerous invertebrates can hitchhike undetected.”

The UKHSA said control measures had been implemented to destroy the larvae, and the area would continue to be monitored closely to identify and eradicate any further mosquitoes and larvae.

It advised residents to remove standing water from gardens and outdoor spaces, including from buckets, containers, paddling pools and plant pots, to reduce opportunities for all species of mosquitoes to breed.

articles.title: Something weird's going on at Saturn. Hubble has spotted a 10-sided geometric formation in the planet's clouds | BBC Sky at Night Magazine
articles.excerpt: The Hubble Space Telescope has given astronomers a view of a 10-sided decagon feature in the clouds at Saturn's south pole.
articles.content:
“The most intriguing part to me is that this seems to have just formed recently,” says Amy Simon at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center.

"The question is, why did it suddenly form now when we haven’t seen one before?"

Scientists have spotted a strange, 10-sided feature in Saturn's clouds. The strange decagon was spotted encircling the planet's south pole by the Hubble Space Telescope.

A regular-sided jet pattern has never been observed in Saturn's southern hemisphere before. So what is it and what's going on?

More Saturn science

  • See Webb's incredible image of Saturn and its moons
  • Cassini spacecraft's best images of Saturn
  • Saturn could float on water (yes it's true!)

Shapes in Saturn's storms

Saturn is mostly made of gas – specifically hydrogen and helium – and its atmosphere rages with ferocious winds that can reach speeds of up to 500 miles per hour (800 kph).

Within this stormy atmosphere, a strange 10-sided shape has formed at the south pole.

It's not the first geometric pattern spotted at Saturn. Astronomers have previously spotted a similar 8-sided shape at its north pole: Saturn's famous hexagon storm.

But, say scientists, the 10-sided shape at the south pole is distinctly different, meaning we may be seeing a new atmospheric phenomenon developing on the ringed planet.

Planetary scientists were able to observe the 10-sided pattern develop over time by looking at years of Hubble Space Telescope observations dating back to 2023.

The discovery was made because Saturn’s changing seasons have slowly brought the planet’s south pole back into view from Earth.

That's when astronomers first spotted it.

Teasing out Saturn's decagon

Agustín Sánchez-Lavega of the University of the Basque Country in Spain and lead author of the study, first spotted hints of Saturn's decagon via the university's Planetary Virtual Observatory Laboratory website.

The site collects images of Solar System planets captured by observers all over the world.

In 2024, Sánchez-Lavega and amateur astronomers Trevor Barry and Jean-Paul Oger noticed a subtle band along Saturn's southern pole.

Additional 2025 imagery from the ground hinted they were in fact looking at a decagon storm on Saturn.

Hubble’s vantage from space gave the team the views they needed to compete the picture.

"Given Saturn’s symmetry in its north-south jet stream system, we have been searching for a counterpart to Saturn’s northern hexagon on the south pole in Hubble images since 1990," says Sánchez-Lavega.

"Images from the Cassini spacecraft, which orbited Saturn between 2004 and 2017, showed no inkling of a long-lived formation, either. The Hubble data confirmed the feature’s presence back to 2023."

What is the feature and how did it form?

The wave is located within one of Saturn’s jet streams and stretches far below the planet's cloud tops through multiple layers of the atmosphere.

It's not just a cloud-level feature, but a large atmospheric structure.

The decagon’s position appears to shift because Hubble has gathered multiple images in different wavelengths of light, giving astronomers views of different altitudes in Saturn’s atmosphere.

"We’ve never seen anything quite like this in Saturn’s southern hemisphere," says Amy Simon, study co-author.

"The northern hexagon has been there every time we’ve looked for more than 40 years. This feature is different – it appears to be strengthening, giving us the rare opportunity to watch a giant atmospheric pattern develop.

The team say further study is required from Hubble and the James Webb Space Telescope.

And the team will also study computer models to try and work out how the decagon formed, how long it will last and how it compares to the hexagon at Saturn's north pole.

articles.title: Hugging Face approached Nvidia's Huang about an acquisition weeks ago, CEO tells CNBC
articles.excerpt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that with Hugging Face, the chipmaker will "expand access to AI for developers and institutions worldwide."
articles.content:
In this article

Nvidia has officially agreed to buy open-source artificial intelligence platform Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, as the chipmaker moves beyond hardware and further up the AI stack.

With the deal, which has been expected since The Information reported on it last week, Hugging Face will "remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang wrote in a blog post on Thursday.

"Together, we will scale Hugging Face's platform, strengthen its infrastructure and expand access to AI for developers and institutions worldwide," Huang wrote.

Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue told CNBC on Thursday that the company approached Huang over the summer about a deal, "and a few weeks later, here we are."

"During the summer, I think we realized that Hugging Face and open source AI in general was at the turning point, and that it needed more, more resources, more scale, more visibility," he told CNBC's Becky Quick on "Squawk Box."

Delangue said he approached first because Nvidia was "a perfect home" for his company, adding that discussions went quite fast to get a deal done.

The acquisition marks Nvidia's second biggest on record, following the $20 billion purchase of assets from chipmaker Groq in December. Prior to that, its largest deal was the purchase of Israeli chipmaker Mellanox for almost $7 billion in 2019.

Nvidia has become the world's most valuable company due to the insatiable demand for its graphics processing units, which have powered the generative AI boom. Hugging Face marks a big bet on a popular AI platform, as Nvidia continues to show that it's more than just a chip company.

Hugging Face was recently at the center of a hacking incident that raised concerns about the rapid evolution of powerful AI and cybersecurity tools.

Delangue, a proponent of open-source models, blamed engineering mistakes for the recent attack on Hugging Face and said his company used an Nvidia version of a Chinese open model to resolve it.

"I am honored that Clem came to me as he considered the next chapter of Hugging Face and believed NVIDIA would be a great home for the company, its community and the future of open models," Huang wrote in Thursday's post.

A woman who was hit by a taxi on Aigburth Road was "immediately worked on" by strangers before she was rushed to hospital. Emergency services arrived at the scene at the pedestrian crossing near Fulwood Road in south Liverpool around 5.40pm after a woman was ht by a white Toyota Voxy private hire taxi on the carriageway travelling towards the city.

The ECHO was told how several strangers near the scene ran over to the woman, who landed on the grass verge in the middle of the road, where they performed CPR on her in the immediate aftermath. One woman, whose partner was at the scene when the incident happened, said: "The taxi hit her and it was left parked in the outside lane with the woman on the grass verge.

"I'm not sure how she got there, whether she was moved or that's where she landed. People ran over straight away and started working on her. The air ambulance was overhead but it was struggling to land, I think it had to land some distance away.

"The people were working on her until the ambulance arrived. The road didn't reopen until about 11pm. I don't know who was there helping except for one woman who lives round the corner [on Fulwood Road]."

The woman who was injured in the incident was rushed to hospital where she died from her injuries.

A spokesperson for Merseyside Police said the taxi driver, a 41-year-old man, stopped at the scene and was arrested on suspicion of causing death by careless or inconsiderate driving whilst under the influence of drugs and is currently in custody.

After police arrived, a large cordon was put in place on the road, with several police vehicles in attendance.

An investigation is underway, with CCTV and witness enquiries underway in the area.

Detective Sergeant Andy Roper from our Matrix Serious Collision Investigation Unit said: “First and foremost my thoughts and those of my team remain with woman’s family at this sad time.

"Road death causes devastation for all those involved and it is our absolute priority to get answers for her family.

“An investigation has been launched to ascertain the circumstance of this collision and we are following up a number of lines of enquiry including speaking to potential witnesses and examining CCTV in the area.

“Aigburth Road is a very busy road and we know at that time there would have been a large volume of vehicles including buses, taxis and delivery drivers, together with pedestrians, in the area.

"I would urge anyone who may have witnessed the incident or was travelling in the area at the time with a dashcam fitted to their vehicle to make contact with our team so that we can check if it has captured anything which may provide answers surrounding this collision.

“Also, if you live in the area and have a CCTV system or Ring doorbell, I would be grateful if you could check your footage to see if you captured anything."

Anyone with information on the incident should contact Merseyside Police Serious Collision Investigation Unit on 0151 777 5747 quoting incident reference 26000720150. Alternatively contact the social media desk via X @MerPolCC or on Facebook ‘Merseyside Police Contact Centre’. You can also report information via our website: https://www.merseyside.police.uk/ro/report/ocr/af/how-to-report-a-crime/ or.Alternatively, contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111, or via their website here: https://crimestoppers-uk.org/give-information/forms/give-information-anonymously In an emergency always call 999.

Tess Daly and Vernon Kay have reunited on a family holiday, months after they announced their split after 22 years of marriage.

Earlier this year, the pair released a joint statement sharing that they had “made the decision to separate amicably”, adding that there were “no other parties involved in this decision”.

The former Strictly Come Dancing host, 57, and Radio 2 DJ, 52, share daughters Phoebe, 21, and Amber, 17, and said that they would “remain great friends and, most importantly, [were] fully committed to our roles as loving and supportive parents”.

In an Instagram carousel uploaded by Daly on Wednesday, 2 September, the family of four can be seen enjoying some quality time together on holiday in France.

In one snap, the parents and their two girls can be seen smiling for a photo whilst sitting at a restaurant.

Other pictures include the 57-year-old posing as she stands on the deck of a yacht, a mirror selfie of Daly and eldest daughter Phoebe, and Daly sitting on a wall overlooking a town.

“Last blast of South of France summer with the fam,” Daly captioned the post which she shared to her more than 900,000 followers.

Friends and fans flocked to the comments to praise the couple for still spending time as a family despite their separation.

“Love that you all stick together. So cool and inspirational,” wrote former Made In Chelsea star Georgia Toffolo, whilst Girls Aloud’s Kimberley Walsh commented a series of love hearts.

One fan wrote: “Tess, Vernon, really pleased to see this, you are an inspiration,” whilst another added: “I wish more families could be like that ,they love their children the kids don’t have to choose perfect result for them all.”

The pair met while working as up-and-coming TV presenters for rival channels in 2001, crossing paths at a BBC Christmas party.

Kay proposed on Christmas Day 2002 at Daly’s parents home, and the pair married the following September near his hometown of Bolton, just 20 miles from where Daly grew up in Stockport.

Sharing the news of their split earlier this year, the pair wrote in an Instagram post: “After much consideration, and with a deep sense of care and respect for one another, we have made the decision to separate amicably.

articles.title: The Longreads Questionnaire, Featuring Jon Ronson - Longreads
articles.excerpt: The author of The Castle likes his music in a time capsule and silence in his home—but definitely not in his stories.
articles.content:
“I do unashamedly want to write page-turners,” Jon Ronson told The New Yorker in an interview. “I can never understand why most nonfiction books have such limited creative ambitions.” Ronson, who is “not a thrill-seeker,” then recounts fearing for his life while being pursued by members of a secretive political gathering—a chase that found its way into Them: Adventures with Extremists, his 2001 breakthrough book. Thrills have a way of finding Ronson, either through active pursuit or some subtler means of revelation. The Men Who Stare At Goats begins with a US Army general who attempts to walk through walls, repeatedly smacking into them. In the opening of The Psychopath Test, a neurologist hands Ronson a baffling package, copies of which have been anonymously mailed to academics throughout the world. The pages turn themselves.

Ronson’s latest, The Castle, earned a starred review from Publisher’s Weekly, which praised the book as “a blockbuster portrait of men gone mad” and Ronson’s style as “intuitive but rigorous.” His podcast, Things Fell Apart, was recently renewed for a third season, in which Ronson will shift focus from American culture wars to individual battles against institutions. He once told The Guardian, “I get called faux-naïf all the time. But I honestly think I am just genuinely naive.” It’s an observation that reminds me of Joan Didion’s own famous self-assessment: that she was “so physically small, so temperamentally unobtrusive . . . that people tend to forget that my presence runs counter to their best interests.” Ronson is warmer than that, but his access is no less astonishing. Time and again, someone allows him to get very close—closer, perhaps, than they might be aware of. Each of Ronson’s books is a testament to his depth of inquiry, his proximity to the surprising, and his conviction that a good narrative should be propulsive.

—Brendan Fitzgerald

Where did you grow up?

Cardiff, Wales. In a suburb called Lisvane.

What places feel like home?

London, for sure. As a child, when we’d visit my grandparents, I’d sneak away and jump on a bus and just get lost in the City. Even when it wasn’t home, it felt like home. Eventually I lived there for decades, loving especially Soho and Islington. I also love our tiny town in the Hudson Valley. We’ve lived here since 2019.

Other than family members, who or what has shaped you the most?

As a teenager, watching Nick Broomfield documentaries and reading the great nonfiction adventurers from the ’60s and ’70s like Hunter S. Thompson and PJ O’Rourke and the writers featured in Tom Wolfe’s The New Journalism. And when I started in journalism, the editors who first gave me a break: Ian Parker, Chris Heath, Deborah Orr, Ian Katz.

What is your favorite time of day?

Early morning. I make a coffee and for the first few hours my brain is at its best and I can write a lot.

What are you really good at?

Narrative nonfiction. If I go off on some journey, I know exactly how to make it work. It’s the only thing I’m good at.

What’s the best gift you’ve ever received?

Recently the BBC gave me a subscription to Descript, a text-based audio editing program. It’s a dream gift for a detail-oriented storyteller. I can finally do the audio editing myself. I sit there for hours.

Describe your favorite meal.

I guess some kind of salad with lots of fruit and vegetables and a good dressing. You can’t beat Greek dressing.

Sound or silence? (And if sound, what sound?)

Silence! I can’t believe how great the silence is here in the Hudson Valley. There’s something very comforting about knowing it won’t end. They’ll never turn this country lane into a big road.

Where do you do your best thinking?

When I’m out on a story, in some strange place, gathering material. I just instinctively know what’ll work, what the best moments are. Fiction people can do that in their imaginations. I can’t. But when I’m out on a story, I just know.

What journey—physical, creative, intellectual, or otherwise—has meant the most to you?

The journey of leaving Cardiff and moving to London when I was 18. I felt like finally my life could begin.

Where do you like to read?

I listen to audiobooks when I’m out walking.

What’s the last rabbit hole you disappeared into?

The Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC). I went to the cage match on the White House South Lawn for GQ, because it was theme-adjacent to my new book The Castle. So I watched all manner of fighter interviews and UFC super-fan videos for that.

Name three publications you enjoy reading these days.

The New Yorker, The Guardian, The New York Times.

What’s one longread that you can’t stop thinking about?

“Andrew Tate’s Empire Of Abuse” was the last one I listened to from beginning to end.

What was the last book you read?

Shakespeare: The World as Stage by Bill Bryson. I listen to it over and over to get to sleep. So I still don’t know how he dies.

What piece of nonfiction are you most proud of writing?

Every book I’ve written has chapters I’m equally proud of: sneaking into Bohemian Grove with Alex Jones and getting chased by the Bilderberg Group in Them, the goat staring in The Men Who Stare At Goats, pretty much all of The Psychopath Test, much of Lost at Sea, Justine Sacco in So You’ve Been Publicly Shamed. The Castle feels really good. I felt very confident writing it, mixing up tones and styles in a way I don’t think I could have managed before.

What’s your most reliable way to get creatively unstuck?

Just wandering around Reddit can be good. The whole world is somewhere on Reddit. And if you don’t find your next story, it might still unlock some part of your brain.

Who’s a writer you turn to when you need some inspiration?

Kurt Vonnegut, for his brevity and his clashes between comedy and horror.

What words do you overuse?

It used to be “There was a silence” but I’ve cured myself of that, thank God.

What’s your favorite guilty pleasure?

I don’t know if this counts, but every book I read for pleasure is a celebrity memoir, mostly musicians and actors. Cher. Anthony Hopkins. Bruce Springsteen. I LOVED the English actor Kathy Burke’s one, A Mind Of My Own. Right now it’s Johnny Marr.

What superpower would you like to have? 

I think I’d like to be able to shoot fire out of my hands. No. Teleportation through space and time.

What animal or nonhuman being do you most identify with?

I really identified with my dog, Floppy—how he wanted to be around people but didn’t want to interact with them.

If you have a free solitary hour in your day, what do you typically do?

Run or walk.

What five items would you place in a time capsule?

Talking Heads’ Stop Making Sense. The Pitt. Succession. All of NPR’s Tiny Desk Concerts, especially Doechii, Sierra Ferrell, and Chappell Roan. Bruce Springsteen’s 1979 No Nukes concert video. Huh, it’s almost all music. I guess that’s the stuff we should remember. People being their best.

What does your writing space look like?

Jon Ronson’s nonfiction books include So You’ve Been Publicly Shamed, The Psychopath Test, Them: Adventures with Extremists, Lost at Sea, and The Men Who Stare At Goats. They have all been international and/or New York Times bestsellers and have been translated into more than 30 languages. His latest book, The Castle, is now available.

articles.title: B&Q, Five Guys and Serco among firms shamed for paying staff below minimum wage
articles.excerpt: The government is cracking down on employers found not to be paying the legal minimum wage
articles.content:
The government is cracking down on employers found not to be paying the legal minimum wage

The government has publicly named hundreds of businesses after they failed to pay staff the National Minimum Wage.

Following "robust" enforcement measures, approximately £4 million in lost earnings has been reimbursed to over 27,000 workers across 658 companies.

Ministers stated that they were resolved to prevent employers short changing their staff, revealing that fines totalling £7 million have been handed to organisations caught paying below the legal minimum wage.

The government confirmed its commitment to publishing these naming lists on a more regular basis, ensuring firms are swiftly held to account and make prompt improvements.

Among the firms named by the government was DIY giant B&Q, which was reported to have failed to pay £456,934 to 4,530 workers.

A spokesperson for the company said: “The shortfalls in payments were unintentional. They relate to calculations involving geographical allowances which are paid in addition to minimum hourly rates.

“All affected colleagues were quickly paid in full in July 2025.”

Other firms named by the Government included:

  • Elysium Healthcare Holdings Limited, reported to have failed to pay £330,048 to 1,095 workers.
  • St George’s, Epsom and St Helier Hospital Group, Epsom, (£123,331 to 75 workers).
  • Support Staff Services Limited, Slough (£119,715 to 323 workers).
  • Five Guys JV Limited, Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea, (£54,642.47 to 3,699 workers).
  • Forest Holidays Ltd (£100,308 to 598 workers).
  • St George’s University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (£77,498 to 55 workers).
  • Lanes Group Limited, Leeds (£67,893 to 297 workers).
  • Serco Limited, Thetford (£36,303.02 to 374 workers.
  • UK Care Team Ltd, Leicester (£67,082 to 99 workers).

It is understood St George’s, Epsom and St Helier maintain that no staff were underpaid as it related to a technical compliance issue where part of their salary for a non tax-deductible “salary sacrifice” (for example, towards childcare) was not counted towards the national minimum wage, even though their gross salary was above the national minimum wage.

The hospitals have changed their process and improved compliance.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said: “The best businesses know that looking after your workers isn’t just the right thing to do, it’s the smart thing to do, building the stronger, more successful businesses that drive growth in every postcode.

“Most employers already understand this, and I want to work with them to ensure they have every piece of guidance and support available to help them follow the rules.

“Short-changing your staff isn’t a shortcut to success and we are determined to stamp it out.”

Minister for the future of work Kate Dearden said: “Underpaying your staff is illegal, and we will not let workers foot the bill for their boss failing to follow the rules.

“We’re making sure workers get the hard-earned pay they deserve, and where employers fall short, they will be held to account.

“Every employer should check their payroll now and reach out to Acas if they need further support.”

TUC general secretary Paul Nowak said: “Bosses who fail to pay the minimum wage deserve to be named and shamed.

“There is no excuse for workers being cheated out of the minimum wage. It’s bad for workers, families and the economy.

“Every pound taken from a worker’s pocket is a pound that could have been spent in local shops, cafes and high streets.

“That’s why the Government’s new Fair Work Agency is so important. It is a chance to come down hard on rogue employers who refuse to do right by their staff.”

articles.title: Simple Minds Announce New Album ‘Sacrosanct’ And Share ‘Beginner Boys’
articles.excerpt: Simple Minds announce new album Sacrosanct, out January 29, 2027 via BMG, and share new single “Beginner Boys” ahead of their biggest arena tour to date.
articles.content:
Simple Minds have announced their brand new studio album Sacrosanct, set for release on January 29, 2027, via BMG. The album follows 2022’s Top 5 record Direction Of The Heart and arrives after a busy period for the band, including a critically acclaimed career-spanning documentary, a joint memoir and a hugely successful global tour.

Last year, Simple Minds played to more than 1.5 million people, including some of their biggest audiences since 1985. It was during this period, energised by touring, that Jim Kerr and Charlie Burchill began crafting and recording the new album.

The band’s 2025 North American tour inspired Kerr and Burchill to draw on their art-rock and new wave roots after seeing fans in cities they had never previously played respond strongly to early songs such as “Sons And Fascination”.

That atmosphere runs through Sacrosanct, an eight-track album described as one of the band’s most vital records in decades, recapturing the magic and majesty at the heart of Simple Minds.

The first song to be released from the album is “Beginner Boys”, inspired by Kerr watching his twin grandsons grow up and thinking about what it means to raise a good man today.

Kerr said the song considers “how strength, tenderness, courage, and gentleness might still belong together, even when the wider culture around them can send mixed signals. It’s less a statement than a question I hope they’ll spend their lives answering for themselves.”

The album opens with “Elysium”, a track inspired by Magazine and named after the paradise of Greek myth. Its natural counterpoint is “King Of The Underworld”, inspired by the figure of Mephistopheles and the forces that rule over human appetites.

Elsewhere, “Jerusalem (State Of Mind)” is influenced by William Blake’s vision of Jerusalem as a longing for a better world, while “Our Secrets Are The Same” explores the lifelong bond between Kerr and Burchill, who met on a Glasgow street as eight-year-olds and have remained creative partners ever since.

The album’s most direct pop moment comes with “Songs”, a celebration of the power of music to lift people on good days and pull them out of darker ones.

The closing tracks, “Alive In This Moment” and “The Next Right Thing”, both deal with nostalgia from different perspectives. The former is about resisting the urge to reach back and instead remain present, while the latter reflects on the passing of time and the loss of those we love.

Speaking about the album title, Kerr said: “We called the album Sacrosanct because after a lifetime of doing this — nearly fifty years of writing songs together — it’s stopped feeling like a career and started feeling like something closer to faith. Calling the record Sacrosanct isn’t an exaggeration. It’s just honest.”

He added: “Making records and performing live is as much part of our lives now as when we started out. We feel grateful to those who support new music from Simple Minds and look forward to seeing you all on our upcoming world tour.”

The metalwork on the album artwork comes from a collaboration between Simple Minds and Glasgow-born sculptor Andy Scott, who has reimagined the band’s logo in steel. Scott, best known for The Kelpies in Falkirk, was awarded an OBE in this year’s King’s Birthday Honours for services to sculpture and fine art.

The release of Sacrosanct will coincide with Simple Minds’ biggest arena tour to date. The tour begins in Australia and New Zealand in February before heading to Europe and the UK in April and May.

The Simple Minds V Tour 2027 promises a panoramic live experience, celebrating five decades of music from a band who continue to evolve while maintaining the energy that has defined their career.

Before the 2027 tour begins, Simple Minds will headline the Sunday night of BBC Radio 2’s In The Park at City Park, Stirling, Scotland, on September 13.

articles.excerpt: Vice City’s unmistakable style comes to life in these two new limited-edition DualSense wireless controller designs.
articles.content:
Vice City’s unmistakable style comes to life in these two new limited-edition DualSense wireless controller designs.

Vice City has a style all its own. From its sun-soaked streets to its bright neon lights, the city will be Leonida’s ultimate destination when players jump into Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19. 

At today’s State of Play, we shared a first look at two new limited edition DualSense wireless controllers inspired by Grand Theft Auto VI which capture that unmistakable Vice City energy: DualSense Wireless Controller – Grand Theft Auto VI Black Limited Edition and DualSense Wireless Controller – Grand Theft Auto VI White Limited Edition.

The black and white limited-edition DualSense wireless controllers each capture the essence of Vice City, from bright days along the coast to vibrant city nights. Both editions feature a shimmering, color-shifting finish that brings together the hues of a Vice City sunset and the glow of neon lights. They both also feature custom palm tree details molded directly into the controller, adding a unique tactile element alongside official Grand Theft Auto VI branding.  

The DualSense Wireless Controller – Grand Theft Auto VI White Limited Edition embodies Vice City at daybreak, from its white sands and pastel skies to all its laid-back glamour.  The DualSense Wireless Controller – Grand Theft Auto VI White Limited Edition will be available in limited quantities globally at direct.playstation.com and at participating retailers.

The DualSense Wireless Controller – Grand Theft Auto VI Black Limited Edition captures the energy of Vice City’s iconic nightlife. The DualSense Wireless Controller – Grand Theft Auto VI Black Limited Edition will be available in limited quantities exclusively through direct.playstation.com where available* and in other regions through select retailers.

In Grand Theft Auto VI, the DualSense wireless controller’s haptic feedback and adaptive triggers instantly respond to the action and provide dynamic resistance, bringing the sights, sounds and sensations of Jason and Lucia’s story to life in your hands. Find out more on how Grand Theft Auto VI plays best on PS5 when it launches on November 19 and check out Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look here.

Both limited-edition DualSense wireless controllers will launch starting on November 19 for a recommended retail price of $84.99 USD/ ¥12,480 (including tax) / €84.99/ £74.99.** Pre-orders start September 10 at 10:00am Local time.

When ordering directly from PlayStation, enjoy free launch day delivery for eligible pre-orders.

articles.title: Building on 30 years of play: First look at the LEGO® PlayStation™
articles.excerpt: Available from October 1, the LEGO set replica of the original PlayStation console is packed with iconic details.
articles.content:
Available from October 1, the LEGO set replica of the original PlayStation console is packed with iconic details.

Today at State of Play, we shared the first look at an all-new collaboration with the LEGO Group – the LEGO PlayStation – that celebrates the games, experiences, and the feelings of play we have shared as a community for over 30 years.

For the first time, players and LEGO fans will be able to create a LEGO replica of the original PlayStation console and PlayStation controller. Brick by brick, this 1,911-piece set represents a near 1:1 scale of the console, measuring 10.5 inches / 26 cm wide when fully assembled. 

To bring this set to life, we collaborated closely with LEGO designers to craft a building experience that is inspired by PlayStation’s origins. When building the set, players will notice hidden details from PlayStation’s history and references to two iconic games that launched on the original PlayStation console, Ape Escape and Gran Turismo. Each diorama features customizable elements – Gran Turismo includes a miniature track complete with scaled down cars, while the Ape Escape diorama has a nostalgic island scene with a swappable blue or red light on the monkey’s helmet. The interactive set has functional mechanisms for the console’s Power and Open buttons, a controller that can plug into the console, and the ability to remove both game dioramas so they can be displayed separately.

The LEGO PlayStation will be available directly from PlayStation on direct.playstation.com starting October 1, 2026, in the U.S., U.K., France, Germany, Austria, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Italy, Spain, and Portugal. The set will also be available from October 1, 2026, for LEGO Insiders Early Access and for all via LEGO.com and LEGO Stores from October 4, 2026. The recommended retail price (RRP) is $179.99 USD | €159.99 EURO | £139.99 GBP | ¥27,980 JPY (including tax). 

Whether you have been with PlayStation since 1994 or are a newer fan, we hope you enjoy building a piece of PlayStation history with this upcoming LEGO set. Learn more about the LEGO PlayStation on LEGO’s official website: LEGO.com/PlayStation.

articles.title: Jin Sakai returns in Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted
articles.excerpt: Plus a fresh look at the brand new narrative expansion, Ghost of Yōtei: Echoes of Sekigahara.
articles.content:
Plus a fresh look at the brand new narrative expansion, Ghost of Yōtei: Echoes of Sekigahara.

Just revealed in State of Play, Jin Sakai will be one of our playable characters in Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted! We are so excited to have the hero of Ghost of Tsushima back for this new mode, complete with all four of his signature stances.

In case you missed our announcement last month, Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted is a brand new single-player combat survival mode that’s included in Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition. 

Most Wanted is our spin on a roguelike. You’ll choose from four playable characters and accept bounties with escalating difficulty. As you complete runs, you’ll earn perks and upgrades to build out your character, becoming more powerful as you go.

It was important to us to make Most Wanted feel like an extension of Ghost of Yōtei’s core combat systems. We want playing through runs to take the familiar weapons and systems you’re used to and turn them into a fresh experience that lets you experiment with characters and builds to find the loadout that works best for you.

So how does it work? To start a run, you’ll select a bounty from the bounty board. Each one features a different member of the Yōtei Six, but to get to them you’ll have to take on waves of enemies and minibosses. As you finish each wave, you’ll unlock perks that help you create a powerful build to eventually take on the final boss of the bounty you’ve selected. Bounties can be replayed at increasing difficulty levels, all culminating in the hardest bounty against Lord Saito himself. 

You’ll also earn Mon as you play, which you can spend outside of runs to unlock new techniques, weapon upgrades, charms, and character unlocks. Plus, any cosmetics you earn through playing Most Wanted will also be unlocked in the main game, so you can wear them during Atsu’s original quest for vengeance, or as you take on the new story expansion in Ghost of Yōtei: Echoes of Sekigahara. 

Once you’ve unlocked all four characters, you can select between them. Each character will start with a katana, as well as their own additional unique weapons, abilities, Ultimates, and Kill Streaks. We encourage you to try them all as each one brings their own different approach to taking down the enemies standing in your way.

Your default starting character will be Atsu, who uses dual katana as well as two Ghost Tools: Metsubushi (Blinding Powder) and a Blind Bomb. Atsu’s Ultimate is “Call of the Pack,” which allows her to summon two wolves to take down nearby enemies, and her Kill Streak is Onryō’s Howl, which will terrify all nearby enemies and force one to flee. 

You’ll also be able to play as Oyuki, who fights with the kusarigama, kunai, and the tanegashima (rifle). Oyuki’s Ultimate is “Shadow Killer,” which unleashes smoke to allow her to quickly assassinate two nearby enemies. Her Kill Streak is Shadow Shinobi, which summons a Nine Tails ally to fight alongside her (and execute their own assassinations) for a limited time. 

The next playable character is Nagato, who uses the yari (spear), tanzutsu (pistol), yumi (long bow), and hankyu (short bow). His Ultimate is “Gambler’s Mark,” which targets two enemies and fires a guaranteed headshot, and his Kill Streak is Blast Arrow, which refills his Concentration and grants an explosive arrow.

Finally, Jin Sakai is our fourth playable character. For Jin, our animation and character art teams worked hard to take his Ghost of Tsushima model and keep it faithful while also applying upgrades for Ghost of Yōtei. Jin can use his katana with all four of the original stances from Ghost of Tsushima, helping to exploit enemy weaknesses. He also starts with a Sticky Bomb and hankyu. Jin’s Ultimate is the “Dance of Wrath” skill from Ghost of Tsushima, which targets multiple enemies and disarms them, and his Kill Streak is, of course, Ghost Stance, which allows him to terrify the enemies around him and kill a limited amount of them in a single hit. 

Beyond selecting the character you want to play as, the real way to create your unique build in Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted is by selecting perks. As you progress through a run, you’ll frequently select between new perks including weapon mastery, gear loadouts, summons, parries, survivability, and more. These are the cornerstone of crafting the perfect build and lead to some of the most exciting surprises as you find the challenge or unexpected value that comes from mixing and matching perks.

In addition to our Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted trailer and Jin Sakai reveal, we also released a new look at Ghost of Yōtei: Echoes of Sekigahara in State of Play Japan today. 

Echoes of Sekigahara is split between two periods of Atsu’s life: her time on the mainland in the massive Battle of Sekigahara, and the present day. In Sekigahara, you’ll learn about Atsu’s history with Nagato, a key figure from her past who fought alongside her. 

In the present, Nagato has arrived in Ezo and is wanted by the Vipers, outlaws loyal to the Snake left leaderless after his death. The Vipers are a group of vicious poachers who have taken over Ashoro Foothills, a previously unseen area of Ezo that was once teeming with wildlife and has now been left devastated.  

Atsu must reluctantly team up with Nagato to find a close ally who’s been taken from her by the Vipers. In Ashoro Foothills, she’ll find new enemy types, new heavy weapons to wield, new mythic tales and abilities, new armor sets and cosmetics, and much more.

If you already own Ghost of Yōtei, you can pre-order the Complete Edition Upgrade for $14.99, which will grant you access to Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted and Ghost of Yōtei: Echoes of Sekigahara on October 1, and instant access to all of the in-game content previously included in the Ghost of Yōtei Digital Deluxe Edition, as well as the Charm of Hokkyokusei.1 If you pre-order by September 30, you’ll also receive an early unlock of the Sakai Armor for Atsu to wear on October 1 without having to unlock it by playing Most Wanted first.1 

If you haven’t played Ghost of Yōtei yet, you can purchase Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition digitally now for $69.99 for instant access to the original Ghost of Yōtei game, plus our online co-op mode Ghost of Yōtei Legends, all of the content in the Ghost of Yōtei Digital Deluxe Edition and the Charm of Hokkyokusei, and access to Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted and Ghost of Yōtei: Echoes of Sekigahara when they launch on October 1. 

Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition also includes new photo mode stamps, additional cosmetics for New Game Plus, and new Trophies for both Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted. If you purchase digitally by September 30, you’ll also get an early unlock of the Sakai Armor on October 1. The physical edition of Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition will launch October 1. 

In case you missed our announcement last month, we’ll also have some updates coming in a free patch for Ghost of Yōtei on October 1, even if you don’t purchase the Complete Edition upgrade.1 All Ghost of Yōtei owners will unlock the free Beauty of Yōtei mode, which allows you to browse the beautiful environments of Ezo and explore them in Photo Mode. All Ghost of Yōtei owners will also receive new tracks for Watanabe Mode that can be experienced anywhere in the game where the mode is enabled, as well as a new option to keep an armor set’s appearance while using a different set’s stats, and a new high contrast accessibility option.

With less than a month to go now, we are so excited to celebrate Ghost of Yōtei’s one-year anniversary with the launch of Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition, and can’t wait for you all to play through Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted and Ghost of Yōtei: Echoes of Sekigahara. Make sure to tag us in all of your Photo Mode creations and your best Most Wanted builds!

articles.content:
In Brief:

  • Father accused of leaving twin babies in car allegedly gave them melatonin
  • Father was released from custody on Wednesday, on the condition he cannot have contact with the children
  • Records show the mother had lost custody of the children
  • CYFD said it will complete the investigation in this case, and the children remain with a family member

ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. – Prosecutors said a man accused of leaving twin baby boys in a hot car for more than two hours outside Dirty Bourbon told police he had given them melatonin.

During a hearing on Wednesday, prosecutors asked a judge to hold Stephan Natseway in jail pending trial after police arrested him on child abuse charges.

Police said a security guard found the babies inside the closed vehicle early Sunday morning, more than two hours after Natseway entered the bar.

Prosecutors told the judge they believe Natseway gave the twins melatonin based on comments he made while sitting in the back of an Albuquerque Police Department vehicle.

The defense argued the case is frivolous and said Natseway should be released because he is not a danger to the community and has no criminal history.

The defense called it “a boneheaded decision” and argued the evidence shows poor judgment, adding that Natseway needs parenting classes.

Judge Britt Baca released Natseway with one condition: He may not have contact with the boys.

Questions regarding the mother

The state also argued the New Mexico Children, Youth and Families Department gave Natseway multiple referrals for medical appointments for one of the boys and that he did not take the child to those appointments.

Prosecutors said the appointments stemmed from a previous case involving the boys’ mother, who lost custody of the children.

CYFD responds

KOB 4 reached out to CYFD earlier this week. The department said the federal Indian Child Welfare Act applies to the case, meaning CYFD must notify the appropriate tribe or pueblo before completing its investigation.

“The hospital examined the children and discharged them after evaluation. Because the Indian Child Welfare Act applies here, CYFD notified the appropriate tribe or pueblo, which initially exercised jurisdiction to complete the investigation. The children were released to a family member, and tribal social services completed a home visit to ensure safety. After 4:00 PM today, the tribe notified the department that they would not be keeping jurisdiction, so CYFD will complete the investigation. CYFD was notified that the children remain with the family member. “ – Jake Thompson, Communications Director, Office of the Secretary.

KOB 4 also reached out to CYFD regarding several claims prosecutors made in court, they sent us the following statement.

“CYFD previously provided limited information regarding this matter. Upon further review of the confidentiality requirements applicable to this case under the Indian Family Protection Act, CYFD cannot provide additional case specific information regarding the children, their placement, safety planning, services, or the current status of the Department’s involvement.“

Second suspect involved

Orry Morris, Natseway’s friend who was with him at the time, is expected in court Thursday, when a judge will decide whether he will remain in jail pending trial.
